questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
1. Dhammapada, Theragatha, Therigatha and
Jataka texts belong to which Buddhist Canon?
questions.explanation:
Dhammapada, Theragatha, Therigatha and
Jataka texts belong to Khuddaka Nikaya. Khuddaka
nikaya, the fifth division of Sutta Pitaka is a wide range
collection of fifteen Books. Five divisions of Sutta
Pitaka are Digha Nikaya, Majjhima nikaya Samyutta
Nikaya, Anguttara Nikaya and Khuddaka Nikaya.
* Pitaka are ancient Buddhist text. Pitaka are 3 in
number.
1. Sutta Pitaka largest among all Pitaka contains
Religious thought of Buddha.
2. Vinaya-Pitaka- Rules of Buddhist Sangha
3. Abhidhamma Pitaka- Philosophy of Buddhism.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
2.
Which of the following texts is related to Jain
Tradition?
questions.explanation:
Paumachariyam is related to Jainism.
Paumachariyam is the earliest Jain work dealing with
the story of Rama. written by Acharya Vimalsuri in
Prakrit. Dasarath Jataka is a Jataka tale found in
Buddhist
literature
about
the
previous
life
of
Shakyamuni (Gautam Buddha). The Thai national epic
is based on Dasarath Jataka.
Iramavataram is Tamil version of Ramayana composed
by Kamban.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
3.
What was the family emblem of the Gupta
monarchs?
questions.explanation:
The family emblem of the Gupta monarchs
was Garuda. Garuda was Found on many seals of
Gupta rulers. Gupta dynasty was founded by Shri
gupta. Silver coins were issued first time during rule of
Chandragupta I.
 Largest number of coins issued by king Kumara
Gupta.
 Vincent Smith said king Samudragupta Napolean of
India.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
4.
Who is the author of Prabodha-Candrodaya?
questions.explanation:
Prabodha chandrodaya is a Sanskrit play of
11th century composed by Krishna Mishra. Krishna
Mishra
was
contemporary
to
Chandela
king
Kirtivarman. This play was played in Khajuraho
complex. It contain 6 Acts. It was written to teach
Advaita doctrine to those who were interested in Kavya
not in philosophy.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
5.
The
Aitareya
and
Satpatha
Brahmanas
mention the name of which monarch, who
performed the 'Asvamedha' sacrifice along
with the 'Aindra Mahabhisek'
questions.explanation:
The Aitareya and Satapath Brahman mention
the king Para who performed the 'Asvamedha sacrifice
along with' 'Aindra Mahabhishek'. King Para was
associated with Kosala Kingdom.
* Aitareya Brahmana is Brahman text of Rigveda.
* Satpath Brahmana is Brahman text of Yajurveda.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
6.
Rajpura and Dvaraka were important town of
which region?
questions.explanation:
Rajpura and Dvaraka were important town of
Kamboja region. Kamboja was situated in the extreme
north west of India. It's capital was Dvaraka.
Mahabharata mentions the name of Rajpura.
* Avanti- Madhya pradesh
* Kuru- near delhi
* Gandhar- Afghanistan.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
7.
Ottakkuttan did not write about which of the
following king?
questions.explanation:
Ottakkuttan did not write about king Rajaraja
I. Ottakkuttion was tamil court poet of later Chola kings
Vikrama Chola, Kulotunga II and Rajaraja II. He has
written 'ula' poems for these 3 kings. ula poems were
written in honour of Kings. Rajaraja I was great king of
chola dynasty. He adopted Title of "Arimolivarman".
[Exam Date: 28.02.2023] Shift-I

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
8.
Name the inscription which refers to the
construction of a puja-sila-prakara
questions.explanation:
Ghosundi refers to the construction of puja-
sila-prakara. It is written in Brahmi script. Ghosundi
inscription is situated in Rajasthan. It confirms the
ancient reverence of Hindu deities samkarshana and
vasudeva. It was first read by D.R. Bhandarkar.
 Nanaghat inscription was inscribed by Satavahana
queen Naganika. It gives vivid picture of satavahana
dynasty
 Hathigumpha inscription of Kharvela provides info. of
events during rule of Kharvela.
 The Halmidi Inscription (Karnataka) dates back 450
A.D. and it is oldest known inscription with Kannada
character. The 16 line inscription is on rectangular
sandstone.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
9.
The Chariya-Pitaka is a collection of :
questions.explanation:
The Chariya-pitaka is a collection of 35
Jatakas in verse. Chariya Pitaka is Khuddaka Nikay'as
15th lesson. Chariya Pitaka was originally written in Pali
languge. Chariya Pitaka was composed by Bhikshu
Dharmarakshit.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText: 10. Lankavatara is related to
questions.explanation:
Lankavatara is related to Vaipulya sutras.
The Vaipulya sutras designate particular scripture in
Mahayana Known as dharma-s. The nine Dharma-s are
a series of books composed at different periods and
belong to different Persuassions.
nine works are 1. Astasahsrika prajnaparamita 2.
Saddharmapundarika 3. Lalita vistara 4. Lankavatara 5.
Suvarnaprabhasa 6. Gandavyuha 7. Tathagataguhyaka
8. Samadhiraja 9. Dasabhumisvara.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
11. The neolithic sites of Kiari and Giak are
located in
questions.explanation:
The Neolithic sites of Kiari and Giak are
located in Ladakh union territory. Kiari and Giak were
famous for hand made red pottery. Burjahom, chirand
etc. are other Neolithic sites in J&K.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
12. The Ghaggar-Hakra system of river is studied
by
questions.explanation:
The Ghaggar Hakra system of river is studied
by C.E. Oldham. many scholars identified Ghaggar
hakra river with the vaidic saraswati river. Ghaggar
Hakra river was intermittent between India and
Pakistan.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
13. According to A.K. Ghosh which of the
following is not a chrono-cultural element of
the palaeolithic culture complex in India?
questions.explanation:
According to A.K Ghosh Borer Burin is not a
chrono cultural element of the Paleolithic culture
complex in India. Pebble, flake and Flake blades tools
was characteristic of Paleolithic culture. In 1966 A.K.
Ghosh divided Indian Palaeolithic culture mainly in 3
parts-
1. Chopper element
2. Flake elements
3. Flake blade elements

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
14. Who among the following Rajput nobles held
the mansab of 7000/7000 under Aurangzeb?
questions.explanation:
Mirza Raja jai singh was Rajput noble who
held the mansab of 7000/7000 under Aurangzeb.
Despite of victories with all his brothers Aurangzeb did
not secured footing on Mughal throne so he needed
support of leading muslim and Rajput generals. hence
he pardoned Jaswant Singh and promoted Jai Singh as
a commander of 7000 the highest possible rank for any
general.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
15. Which one of the following texts, describes two
methods of lifting water out of wells in India?
questions.explanation:
Baburnama describes two methods of lifting
water out of wells in India. Babur wrote in Baburnama
In Lahore, Dipalpur people lift water by means of
wheel. In Agra, Chandawar, Bayana people lift water
with a bucket at the well-edge they setup fork of wood-
having a roller adjusted between the forks tie a rope to
large bucket put the rope over a roller bucket and tie it's
others and to the bullock one person must drive bullock
another empty Bucket.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
16. Who observed that while Akbar was on an
expedition to Kabul to subdue the rebellion of
Mirza Hakim, he appointed his mother,
Hamida Banu Begam, in charge of the suba of
Delhi.
questions.explanation:
Father Anthony Monserrate observed that
while Akbar was on an expedition to Kabul to subdue
the rebellion of Mirza Hakim he appointed his mother
Hamida Bano Begam in charge of the suba of Delhi.
Father Monserrate reached in Akbar's court with father
Aquaviva
of
Portugal.
Akbar
appointed
father
Monserrate as teacher of prince Murad.
Father Monserrate accompanied Akbar on his military
expedition to Kabul in 1581. Father Monserrate
remained at Akbar's court untill April 1582.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
17. In
January
171,
Muzaffar
Jang
was
accompanied by a French force under the
leadership of which one of the following
commanders.
questions.explanation:
In January 1751- Muzaffar Jang was
accompanied by a French force under the leadership of
captain Bussy. In second carnatic war French East India
company supported Muzaffar Jung's claim on throne in
Hyderabad and chanda sahib's claim on carnatic throne.
French sent force in commandership of Bussy. IInd
Carnatic war extended from 1749-54 A.D.
This war ended with the Treaty of Pondicherry.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
18. In early modern period, who was known as
"Ummal'?
questions.explanation:
In early modern period 'Ummal' was Tax
collector.
Some, other important terms
Muqaddam – village headman Abwab – cess
Diwan-i-wizarat – Finance department
Ghari – House tax
Fawazil – Surplus amount
Muqti – Iqta holder.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
19. Saranjam, assignment of revenue from villages
to support military service, was a popular
practice under which Empire?
questions.explanation:
Saranjam assignment of revenue from
villages to support military service was popular practice
under Maratha empire.
Saranjam system was like Jagir system the land was
mostly in the form of rural watan. its owner being
entitled to extract revenue from the villages included in
territory. Saranjam usually given that person for heroic
deeds in military field.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
20. Who
wrote
'Time
is
precious
and
is
irreplaceable"?
questions.explanation:
"Time is precious and is irreplaceable"
written by Abul Fazal.
Abul fazal was among nine lewels of Akbar. Abul Fazal
composed Akbarnama in 3 volumes. Third volume Ain-
i-Akbari is his most famous book. It contained detailed
report of Akbar's government and administration.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
21. Who stated that the days of Nur Jahan were
revived for her (Lal Kunwar) and coins were
issued in her name?
questions.explanation:
Hadi kamwar khan stated that the Days of
Nur Jahan were revived for her (Cal kunwar) and coins
were issued in her name. Hadi kamwar khan added a
continuation to Jahangir's memoir from 1624 (where
motmid khan stopped) and death in 1627. He was
contemporary of Aurangzeb.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
22. Which one of the following sites in Rajasthan
provides evidence of the onset of aridity around
2000 B.C.
questions.explanation:
Lunkaransar site in Rajasthan provides
evidence of the onset of aridity around 2000 B.C.
Lunkaransar is located in Bikaner District.
Lunkaransar is a Playa lake. Migratory birds came here
in winter season.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
23. The Court of Directors withheld their sanction
to the annexation of which princely state on the
basis of 'Doctrine of Lapse'.
questions.explanation:
The court of Directors withheld their sanction
to the annexation of Karauli princely state on the basis
of doctrine of Lapse. Karauli princely state was in
Rajasthan. Princely state of Karauli was established by
Raja Bijai pal, a yaduvanshi Rajput around 995 A.D
Last ruler of Karauli was Maharaja Ganesh pal deo.
* Satara was first princely state annexed by Doctrine of
Lapse in 1848.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
24. Which Indian Factories Act provided for a
weekly holiday for all workers?
questions.explanation:
The second Indian factory act 1891 provided
for a weekly holidays for all workers. Other provisions
of second factory act
* Minimum age for the employment of children raised
from seven to nine years
* To secure to woman and children proper intervals for
food and rest during day
* To limit the employment of women to eleven hours a
day.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
25. What was the immediate cause for the first
burmese war (1824-6)?
questions.optionA:
The declaration of cachar as a British
protectorate
questions.optionB:
The establishment of political authority by
Burma in Manipur
questions.optionC: The British naval mission in Rangoon
questions.optionD: The British expedition in Misami hills
questions.explanation:
The Immediate cause of EirstAnglo Burmese
war (1824-26) was the declaration of Cachar as a
British Protectorate. The war ended with Treaty of
Yandabo (1820).
Important conditions of treaty
* Pay rupee one crore as war compensation.
* Abandon claims on Assam, Cachar and Jaintia
* Recognise Manipur as an Independent state.
* Accept a British resident at Ava while posting a
Burmese envoy at Calcutta.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
26. Who wrote the essay 'Gandhiji's Leadership and
the Congress Socialist Party'?
questions.explanation:
"Gandhi ji's Leadership and the congress
socialist party" essay was written by Jaiprakash
Narayan. Congress socialist party was founded in 1934
by Jaiprakash Narayan, Ram Manohar Lohia and
Acharya Narendra Dev. It declared it would act under
the aegis of INC. It's primary objective was to Outroot
British imperialism and empowerment of labourers,
farmers and other Vulnerable class of the society.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
27. The celebrated diamond, the Koh-i-Noor, was
surendered to the British crown after which
war?
questions.explanation:
The celebrated diamond Koh-i-Noor was
surrendered to the British crown after Second Anglo-
Sikh war. Second Anglo Sikh war was fought between
Sikhs & British army in 1848-1849. At that time
governor general was Lord Dalhousie. Charles Napier
commander of British army defeated Sikhs in "battle of
Gujarat." Punjab was annexed in British territory
maharaja Daleep Singh sent to London with anuual
pension of 50000 pound.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
28. As a prominent leader of the 1928 scavengers'
strike who was given the epithet 'Dhangarma'
(Mother of Scavengers)
questions.explanation:
As a prominent leader of the 1928 scavengers
strike Prabhabati Das Gupta was given the epithet
"Dhangarma". on 5 March 1928 8000 scavengers went
on strike in Calcutta. Their demands were wage
increase, suitable housing and accommodation 15 days
leave per year. medical benefits and free primary
education for their children. Strike was settled by J.M.
Sengupta Mayor of Culcutta.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText: 29. 'Estado Da India's is popularly known as :
questions.explanation:
Estado Da India' is popularly known as
Portuguese east India company. Estado Da India was
the mane the Portuguese to that part of their empire
which stretched from India to east Asia. Estado Da
India formed in 1505 A.D. Francisco De Almeida
appointed as first viceroy of Portuguese company.
Almeida's vision was to make the Portuguese the master
of Indian Ocean. His policy was known as "Blue water
policy".

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
30. In late 1770s and 1780s Khatbandi regulations
were related to :
questions.optionA:
Indian peasants to buy their agricultural tools
from the British East India Company
questions.optionB:
Bind Indian artisans to sell their products
exclusively to the British East India company
questions.optionC:
Bind Indian peasants to pay their land
revenue in each to the British East India
Company
questions.optionD:
Indian artisans to buy their raw material like
cotton exclusively from the British East India
Company
questions.explanation:
In late 1770s and 1780s khatbandi regulations
were related to Bind Indian Artisans to sell their
products exclusively to the British East India company.
Thus the Artisans were reduced step by step to the
position of Bonded laborers by the denial of free Access
to market by the use of coercion and by laws and
regulations made by company's government. Khatbandi
regulations were passed by Bengal Govt.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
31. Dada Bhai Naoroji presented the case of 'drain
of wealth' from India before which Commission
in 1895.
questions.explanation:
Dada bhai Naoroji presented the case of drain
of wealth from India before welby commission. welby
commission was established by British government In
year 1895 under official name 'Royal commission on
expenditure Administration of India' Main objective of
commission was to find out the income and expenditure
of the nation. Dadabhai Naoroji was the commissions
first Indian member.
 Macdonald Commission – 1900 by curzon to enquire
into the Famine of 1873-74 in Bengal & Bihar.
 Strachey Commission– 1880 first famine commission.
It was established to develop general strategy to tackle
famines.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
32. The Fergusson college was developed from
which institution of 1880s
questions.explanation:
The Fergusson college was developed from
New English school of 1880s. In 1880 V.K. Chiplunkar,
Balgangadhar Tilak and M.B. Namjoshi started new
English school in Pune with the objective of cheapening
and facilitating education. The founders of the
Fergusson college had first started the new English
school, Pune in 1880 and Later established the 'Deccan
Education society in 1884. Fergusson College was
started in 1885.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
33. Who was the President of the 1929 Congress
sub-committee on untouchability?
questions.explanation:
Pandit madan mohan Malaviya was the
president of the 1929 congress sub committee on
untouchability.
Madan Mohan Malviya was educationist social
reformer and freedom fighter. He was elected as the
president of the congress committee (Four times) in
1909, 1918, 1932 and 1933. Mahatma Gandhi gave him
title of 'Mahamana'. Dr. S. Radha Krishnan gave him
status of Karmayogi. He founded Hindu Mahasabha in
1905. He founded Banaras Hindu university in 1916.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
34.
Who was the Propounder of the theory of
'Utilitarianism'?
questions.explanation:
J.S. Mill was Propounder of the theory of
'utilitarianism'. Utilitarianism was a developed in
Britain. Main objective of utilitarianism is "maximum
satisfaction for maximum number of people."

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText: 35. Where was Herodotus born?
questions.explanation:
Herodotus was born in Halicarnassus. now in
Turkey. Herodotus is known as "Father of history".
Herodotus earned this title from Roman statesman.
Cicro because he authored the first authoritative
historical text that systematically recorded historical
events. Herodotus wrote books the Histories and The
tale of the great Persian war.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
36. Leni Riefenstahl's film Triumph of the will
deals with ___________.
questions.explanation:
Triumph of the will is a 1935 German Nazi
propaganda film directed and produced by Leni
Riefenstahl's. It chronicles the 1934 Nazi party congress
in Nuremberg. Which was attended by more than
700000 Nazi Supporters. The film contains excerpts
speeches given by Nazi leaders at the congress
including Hitler.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
37. Who said, "As works of the imagination, the
historian's work and the novelist's do not
differ. Where they do differ is that the
historian's picture is meant to be true".
questions.explanation:
R.G. Collingwood said "As works of the
Imagination. the historian's work and the novelist's do
not differ. where they do differ is that the historian's
picture is meant to be true."
R.G. Collingwood was great historian from England. He
is best known for his works "The principles of Art
(1938) and the posthumously Published" "The Idea of
History".

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
38. Who said "History has to be rewritten because
history is the selection of those threads of causes
or antecedents that we are interested in".
questions.explanation:
Oliver Wendell Holmes Jr. said "History has
to be rewritten because history is the selection of those
threads of causes or antecedents that we are interested
in". Oliver Wendell Holmes Jr. was an American Jurist
who served as an associate justice of the supreme court
of the united states from 1902-1932.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText: 39. Ramoshi Rebellion of 1831 was led by whom?
questions.explanation:
Ramoshi Rebellion of 1831 was led by Umaji
Raje. Ramosis, the hill tribe of western ghat resented
the policy of Annexation after the Annexation of
Maratha territories by British. The Ramosis who had
been employed by Maratha administration, lost their
means of livelihood they rose under chittur Singh in
1822. from 1825-26 to 1831 Ramosi rebellion was led
by Umaji Raje

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
40. Raja Rammohan Roy's Brahmo Samaj was a
successor to :
questions.explanation:
Raja Rammohan Roy's Brahmo samaj was a
successor to Atmiya Sabha. In 1814 Raja Rammohan
Roy set up Atmiya Sabha in Calcutta to propagate the
monotheistic ideals of the Vedanta and to campaign
against Idolatary. Caste rigidities, meaningless rituals
and other social ills. In 1828 he founded Brahmo samaj.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
41. Which of the following statements are correct
about Tarikh/Tawarikh during the Medieval
period?

A. They were court chronicles

B. Baburnama is not based on roznamcha
(diaries)

C. The Persian tradition was not influenced
by monarchical institutions

D. They were commemorative venture that
made historiography focal to book writing

E. This pattern was influenced by the
chronicle of the Seljuq Empire.

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below :
questions.explanation:
Statement A.D and E are correct about
Tarikh/Tawarikh during the medieval period that-
* They were court chronicles
* They were commemorative venture that made
historiography focal to book writing
* This pattern was influenced by chronicle of Seljuq
empire.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
42. Regarding to the role of European Trading
Companies which of the following statements
are correct?

A. In 1605, the Dutch captured the Portuguese
fort of Ambonia

B. In 1606, Dutch obtained a farman from the
ruler of Golconda to setup a factory at
Masulipatam.

C. The Dutch opened their factory at Surat in
1617.

D. English had already opened a factory at
Surat in 1625

E. The Dutch captured Malacca in 1639.

Choose the most appropriate answer from the
options given below :
questions.explanation:
Statement (A) (B) and (C) are correct
regarding a role of European Trading companies.
Statement (D) is incorrect because English opened a
factory at Surat in1613 not in 1625.
statement (E) is incorrect because Dutch captured
Malacca in 1641 not in 1639

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
43. Which of the following are correct?

A. The Vayu Purana refers to Vindhyasakti,
founder of Vakataka dynasty and his son
Pravira.

B. In early epigraphic records the Abhiras
figure
as
General
of
the
Saka
Mahakshatrapas of Western india.

C. The Ikshvakus mentioned in the Kautilya
Arthashastra, ruled from the city of
Madurai.

D. The Bodhi dynasty flourished in territory
that was once within the sphere of Chera.

E. The Mahavamsa does not mentioned Chola
king Karikala invasion of Cylone.

Choose the correct answer from the option
given below :
questions.explanation:
Statement (A), (B) and (E) are correct

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)

regarding Naval mutiny 1946.
on 18 February 1946 the ratings of HMIS Talwar in

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
50. Which of these are correct?

A. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar joined as a Professor
at Sydenham College

B. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar founded Independent
Labour Party.

C. Independent Labour Party had a red flag.

shudra identity

book 'The Annihilation of Caste'.

questions.optionD: A, B, C and D only
questions.explanation:
B.R. Ambedkar was born on April 14, 1891
Ambedkar got school education from satara He
completed his graduation from Elphinstone college
Bombay. He got his M.A. and Ph.D. from Columbia
university. Ambedkar joined Sydenham college as a
professor of political economy. He published Bahiskrit
Bharat newspaper, Ambedkar founded Independent
Labour party in 1936. Its flag have red colour.
Ambedkar did not supported a non-Aryan theory of
dalit-shudra identity. In 1936 they published book "The
Annihilation of caste". In 1956 Ambedkar embraced
Buddhism.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)

Hall, Calcutta.

B. Khudiram Bose was executed on 30th April,

wyllie in London on Ist July 1909, statement (B) is not

53. Which of these are correct

A. The Hindi-Urdu controversy began in the
North-Western
provinces
and
Awadh
sometime in the 1860s.

B. The movement acquired greater intensity
in 1890s with the foundation of the 'Nagri
Pracharani Sabha' in 1893.

has greater sprinkling of Sanskrit words.

D. Urdu was written in Persian script thus
had more Persian and Arabic words.

options given below :
questions.optionC: A, B, C and D only
questions.optionD: A, C, D and E only
questions.explanation:
In 1867 Hindus in united provinces of Agra
and Oudh began to demand that Hindi be made an
official language in place of Urdu, Babu Shiva Prasad
was one of early proponents of Nagari script, movement
intensified after establishment of Nagari Pracharini

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)

correct.

into Persian language.

1657 CE.

Yoga Vashisht in 1860.

Dara shikoh was son of Shahjahan he
translated fifty Upanishads into Persian language

the year 1657 CE. His book Majma-ul-Bahrain was
devoted to a revelation of the mystical and pluralistic
affinities between Sufic & Vedantic. He commissioned
translation of Yoga Vasistha in 1006 A.H.

56. Which statement from below are correct?

B. Sariputra and Tathagata are two different

C. Both the Theravadins and Mahayanist

Sarnath, near Varanasi.

Buddhism believes in three jewels Buddha, Dhamma
and Sangha to seek nirvana. Buddha delivered his first
sermon in Sarnath. Sariputra was chief disciple of
Buddha, Ashoka's Lion capital was first installed in

national Amblem of India.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
59. In regard to Bhakti movement, which of the
following statements are correct?

A. Ramanujam wrote devotional poems and
inspired
the
spread
of
devotional
Vaishnavism among the masses.

B. Basava advocated tantric practices and
temples rituals to foster the anti Brahmin
lingayat movement.

C. Vallabhacharya created awareness about
the importance of Krishna Bhakti.

D. Ramdasa popularized the workship of
Vishnu is his avatar as Rama.

E. Namadeva was a famous saint of Bengal.

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below :
questions.explanation:
Bhakti movement spread between 15th to 17th
century A.D. Ramanujam, Vallabhacharya, chaitanya
Basava, Namdev etc were famous saints of Bhakti
movement. Ramanuja wrote devotional poems to spread
Vaishnavism. Vallabhacharya promoted Krishnabhakti.
Ramdasa popularized the worship of Vishnu in his
avatar Rama. Basava founded saiva sect lingayat and
advocated tantric practices. Namdeva was famous saint
of Varkari sect in Maharashtra He lived as devotee of
Lord Vitthal of Pandharpur.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
60. Which of the following are correct?

A. Rani Jindan was kept as a prisoner in
Banaras.

B. Rani Jindan prayed to the king of Nepal to
give her shelter.

C. Dalip Singh embraced Christianity in 1853.

D. Dalip Singh renounced Christianity and re-
embraced the Sikh faith.

E. Dalip Singh died in London.

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below :
questions.optionC: A, B, C and D only
questions.explanation:
Rani Jindan was wife of Ranajit singh and
mother of Dalip singh. She was regent of Dalip singh.
British declared war on sikh empire in Dec 1845 after
the victory in first anglo sikh war. They retained Dalip
singh as ruler but imprisoned Rani Jindan in Benaras.
Rani Jindan escaped Nepal and found asylum by Jung
Bahadur. After second Anglo sikh war Britishers
annexed Punjab and sent Dalip singh London where he
accepted Christianity Later he renounced Christianity
and Dalip singh died in 1893 in Paris.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)

61. Which of the following are correct?

A. Vasudeo Balwant Phadke worked in the
Commissariat
(Military
Accounts)
department for over fifteen years.

B. Phadke was convinced that the miseries of
India were the consequence of foreign rule.

C. Phadke was sent to Andamans jail.

D. Phadke was impressed by the loyalty of
'Dhanagars' to his cause.

E. Phadke did not write an autobiographical
account.

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below :
questions.optionC: A, B, C and D only
questions.explanation:
Vasudev Balvant Phadke born on 4 Nov 1845
in Maharashtra. He graduates from Bombay university.
He worked in commissariat examiner's office for over
15 year's. He decided that only solution to the problem
of India was freeing India from British rule. Phadke
was impressed by the loyalty of Dhangars to his cause.
He was arrested in 1879 and tried in Pune and then
transported for a life sentence to Aden. He died in jail
by disease Tuberculosis.
Phadke wrote his autobiography "mari Jeevan katha"
published by Navajivan trust.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)

A. Bentinck proposed the formation of a Tea
Committee in 1834.

B. The first coffee plantations had been
established at Fort Gloster in Bengal.

C. Minden Wilson states that Francois Grand
started the first indigo factory in Bengal.

D. The production of machine made paper
dates from 1870 when the Bally mills were
established in Bengal.

E. Major Andrew Duncan brought to the
notice of the Madras Government the fine
quality of Salem steel in 1808.

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below :
questions.optionA: A, C, D and E only
questions.optionB: A, B, C and D only
questions.explanation:
Bentinck proposed the formation of Tea
committee in 1834. First coffee plantations has been
established at Fort Gloster in Bengal. First Indigo
factory was set up by Carel blume in India near
Hooghly Bengal in year 1779. Machine made paper
production started from 1870 from Bally mills (Bengal).
First attempt to establish steel factory by Mr. Duncan in
1808 failed miserably.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
63. Which out of the following are correct?

A. The Indian Cinematograph Act was passed
in 1918.

B. In 1920, Censor Boards were set up in the
four towns of Bombay, Calcutta, Madras
and Rangoon.

C. The Dramatic Performances Act was
enacted in 1878.

D. In
Lahore,
the
Censor
Board
was
established in 1927.

E. T.P.O.' Connor acted as the President of
the British Board of Film Censors.

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below :
questions.optionA: A, B, C and D only
questions.optionC: A, B, D and E only
questions.explanation:
The Indian Cinematograph Act was passed in
1918. It made mandatory for exhibitors to secure a
license from local civil authorities to screen a film and
for censorship to precede any film exhibited in India. In
1920 censor Boards were set up in four towns of
Bombay, Calcutta, madras and Rangoon. The dramatic
performance Act was passed in 1876 under. Viceroy
Northbrook. In Lahore, the censor board was
established in 1927. T.P.O Connor was second president
of British Board of film censors.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
64. Which of these are correct?

A. In 1926, the National Council of Women in
India was formed.

B. Lady Mehribai Tata remained main spirit
during the early years of the National
Council of Women.

C. All India Women's Conference came into
existence in 1928.

D. Initially All India Women's Conference
was a non-political body to promote
women's education.

E. Later on All India Women's Conference
got involved in national politics and
lobbied for all sorts of women's rights.

Choose the most appropriate answer from the
options givenbelow :
questions.optionD: A, B, C and E only
questions.explanation:
National council of women in India was
formed in 1925. First president of NCWI was Maharani
of Baroda. Mehribai Tata was key figure in NCWI.
According to Mehribai Tata purdah system, caste
differences and lack of education prevented women
from working to change social condition. All India
women's conference was formed in 1927 by margaret
cousins in order to improve educational efforts for
women and children. Initially it was a non political
body to promote women's education Later on it got
involved in politics and lobbied for all sort's of
women's rights.

that should not be killed on certain day. This pillar edict
also describes release of 25 prisoners.

Read the following passage and answer the
following questions :
Endowments to the Saiyids and their khanqahs,
meant to relief for their families and followers, gave
them control over land. They were fortunate enough to
have fertile zones for farming; they derived income from
the voluntary labour of their disciples on these lands, and
also from gifts of produce from the peasants and artisans
of their area. With the unpaid labour of their disciples,
they accumulated large fortunes. Over a period of time,
the system of religious and secular grants, and the
subjection of peasants and craftsmen to the grantees

96. "From Gujarat to Jammu and from Attock to
Rohilkhand, there is no power but Sindhia and
Sikhs, everything else is but a name. If they
should dispute, the contest will be serious and
important : should they unite, their strength
will be irresistable."

Mahadji Sindhia was honoured with which title
by the Mughal emperor
questions.explanation:
Mahadji scindhiya Throned Shah Alam as
independent ruler on Delhi then shah Alam II honoured
him title of 'Vakil-i-mutlaq' (Prime minister) in 1783.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText: 97. Mahadji Sindhia died in the year
questions.explanation:
Mahadji Scindhia was a Maratha statesman
and ruler of Ujjain in central India. He is reputed for
having restored the Maratha rule over north India and
for modernizing his army. Mahadji Scindhia died in
February 1794.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
98. What is the correct clause of the Treaty of
Salbai (1782)?
questions.optionA:
The Marathas and the british will collaborate
against the Mughals
questions.optionB: British returned Bassein to the Marathas
questions.optionC:
Raghunath Rao relinquished his claim to the
title of Peshwa
questions.optionD:
A convention was signed at Wadgaon
between the British and the Gaekwad as a
part of it.
questions.explanation:
Treaty of salbai was signed between Marathas
and East India company in 1782
conditions of treaty
1. Under it the company retained it's control of Salsette
and Broach. and acquired guarantees that the
Marathas would defeat Hyder Ali of Mysore and
retake territories of Carnatic.
2. Marathas also guaranteed that the French would be
prohibited from establishing settlement on their
territories.
3. Raghunath Rao relinquished his claim to the title of
Peshwa.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
99. During the regime of which Peshwa, the
Maratha state reached its territorial zenith
extending from 'Kattack to Attock"
questions.explanation:
During the regime of Balaji Baji Rao the
Maratha state reached it's territorial zenith extending
from "Kattack to Attock". Balaji Baji Rao was Peshwa
between 1740 to 1761.
Balaji Bajirao maintained control on economy and
increased income of Maratha territory.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I)
questions.questionText:
100. Who followed the policy of expansion of
Maratha from 'Krishna to Attock'?
questions.explanation:
Bajirao I tried to convince Shahu to attack the
Mughals during their declining condition. He dreamt to
fly the Maratha flag from Krishna to Attock
* Bajirao I also known as "Second founder of Maratha
empire".

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-II)
questions.questionText:
1. Alara, the great teacher of the Buddha
belonged to which tribe?
questions.explanation:
Alara, the great teacher of the Buddha belong
to Kalamas of Kesaputta which is now situated in
Kudwar in Sultanpur Distinct siddharth left his home in
age of 29 years. he wandered 7 years in search of
knowledge. after 7 years he come in Ashrama of Alara
kalama (Sankhya Acharya) near vaishali.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-II)
questions.questionText:
2.
Which philosopher of India propounded the
philosophy of Vishishtadvaita?
questions.explanation:
Ramanujacharya Propounded philosophy of
Vishishtadvaita. According to Vishishtadvaita philosophy
Brahman is eternal the soul and material world both
exist only through Brahman. Vishishtadvaita doesn't see
the world as simply illusion, which would make it
separate for Brahman. The material world is part of
Brahman's nature.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-II)
questions.questionText:
3. The critical edition of the Mahābhārata project
was led as General Editor by :
questions.explanation:
The critical edition of the Mahabharata project
was led as General editor by V.S. Sukthankar. He
started this project in 1925 Project finally completed in
1966. English translation of critical edition was
undertaken by J.A.B. Van Buitenen.
* Mahabharata's Persian translation was commissioned
by Akbar. with name Razmnama (Book of war).

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-II)
questions.questionText:
4.
Gaṇḍaraditya was a
questions.optionC: Temple architect of the Chola dynasty
questions.explanation:
Gandaraditya was chola king. Gandaraditya
was son of Parantanka Chola I. He Ruled chola empire
between
950-956
A.D.
Gandaraditya
was
not
expansionist. He was keen in building temples. He was
devotee of lord Shiva and built numerous Shiva
temples. Gandaraditya was poet he composed hymns on
lord Shiva. He composed 'Thiruvisaippa poetic work on
Lord Shiva in Chidambaram temple.'

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-II)
questions.questionText: 5. Which one of these is NOT a jain text?
questions.explanation:
Yamaka is not a Jain text. Yamaka is the
scriptures of a Buddhist monk laws in Pali canon. It is a
text on applied logic and analysis included in
Abhidhamma Pitaka. Nisitha Sutra is part of Acaranga
sutra of Jainism.
Abidhana chintamani is a vocabulary of Jain doctrines
composed by Hemchandra. Tattvarthadhigama sutra is
ancient Jain text composed by Acharya Umaswami. It is
considered first Jain text in Sanskrit.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-II)
questions.questionText:
6.
Who was the founder of Kardamaka dynasty?
questions.explanation:
The founder of Kardamaka dynasty was
chastana, kardamaka's were saka rulers who ruled India
for nearly 300 years. Kardamaka rulers issued silver
coins which bear name and title of the issuing ruler and
his father and coins were continuously dated.
* chastana ruled India during 78-130 CE.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-II)
questions.questionText:
7.
Jinaprabhasuri
in
his
Vividhtirthakalpa
include a section on the holy city of?
questions.explanation:
Jinaprabhasuri in his book Vividhtirthakalpa
include a section on the holy city of Mathura. The
building of Jaina stupa (mathura) has legend associated
with it as mentioned by Jinaprabha suri in his 14th
century text Vividha tirtha kalpa. He says "Two monks
came to Mathura and lodging in a garden converted its
mistress, a goddess, so that compensate for her failure
to the Jain community the stupa there, constructed a
replica of it made out of gold and Jewels. Thus the stupa
is called Devanirmit stupa."
* Vividhatirtha kalpa contains 60 sections on the holy
cities of Jainism.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-II)
questions.questionText:
8.
King Para is associated with kingdom of
questions.explanation:
King 'para' is associated with Kosala
kingdom. Kosala was among 16 Mahajanapadas. It
extended from awadh region to Orissa. Shakya clan
territory developed in kosala- about 500 BCE during the
reign of Prasenjit it was regarded as one of the four
powers of the north.
Shravasti was the capital city of kosala.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-II)
questions.questionText:
9.
Copy of which Asokan Rock Edict is found
engraved on a bowl?
questions.explanation:
Copy of 7th major rock edict is found
engraved on a bowl. 7th rock edict mentioned Tolerance
towards religions among all sects and welfare measures
for the public in his as well as his neighboring
kingdoms.
8th rock edict- mentioned Ashoka's first visit to Bodh
Gaya and the Bodhi tree.
11th rock edict- mentioned Dhamma as the best policy
to follow which includes respect for elders and
concerned for slaves and servants.
13th rock edict- Mentioned victory over kalinga and
gives Vivid picture of the change of Ashoka from an
aggressive and violent warrior to a great lover and
preacher of peace

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-II)
questions.questionText:
10. Name the Buddhist text that shows caste was
NOT rigidly tied to a craft :
questions.explanation:
Dasa Brahman jataka shows caste was not
rigidly tied to craft. Jataka tales were stories of previous
births of Buddha.
* Suttavibanaga is the first book of the Theravadin
Vinaya Pitaka. It is commentary on the community
rules.
* Chullavagga mentioned first and second Buddhist
councils and establishment of the community of
bhikkhunis.
* Kathavattu was authored by Mogaliputta Tissa.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-II)
questions.questionText: 11. Who wrote the book Chatuhsatika?
questions.explanation:
Chatuhsatika was written by Arya Deva.
Arya Deva was a Mahayana Buddhist and disciple of
Nagarjuna and Madhyamaka philosopher. Chatuhstika
was influential work on Madhyamaka in India. and
Tibet. Aryadeva was from Simhala.
* Asanga was founder of the "yogachar school"
* Asvaghosa wrote an epic Buddhacharita and Kavya
saundarananda.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-II)
questions.questionText: 12. The Hathnora specimen belongs to
questions.explanation:
Hathnora specimen belongs to Homo Erectus.
on Dec 5,1982 the geologist Arun Sonakia discovered
the only known fossil of Human ancestor from bank of
Narmada in Hathnora The Narmada human, a fossil
skull belong to category of Homo erectus who inhabited
the earth from 1.8 million to 200000 years ago and
preceded Homo sapiens.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-II)
questions.questionText:
13. The Archeological site of Uttarbaini which
yielded early palaeolithic artefacts is located in
questions.explanation:
The archaeological site of Uttarbaini which
yielded early Paleolithic artefacts is located in Jammu.
Tools found form Uttarbaini dated back 3 to 25 in
Jammu & Himachal belong to same age. Paleolithic
evidence widespread from Jammu to Kangra and lower
Himachal Pradesh & Punjab.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-II)
questions.questionText: 14. Studies on Didwana lake were conducted by
questions.explanation:
In 1971, Gurdip singh a plant pale ecologist
carried out pollen analytical studies of salt lake deposits
(Sambhar, Didwana and Lunkaransar and fresh water
lake Pushkar) in an area centering on Rajasthan desert
in north west India which reflects closely on the nature
of climate of the period of Indus valley civilization.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-II)
questions.questionText:
15. Which leader was instrumental in getting the
smuggled footage of Indian National Army for
a film on Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose?
questions.explanation:
Sardar Vallabh Bhai Patel was instrumental in
getting the smuggled footage of Indian national Army
for a film on netaji.
Samadhi movie released in 1950 is a spy film directed
by Ramesh Saigal on the life of Netaji Subhash Chandra
Bose. It depicts freedom movement also.
In movie named Subhash Chandra released on the
earlier life of S.C. Bose.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-II)
questions.questionText:
16. Which of the following Portuguese Roman
Catholic missionary did notable work in the
field of opening some elementary schools and
some orphanages?
questions.explanation:
Robert-de-nobil Portuguese- Roman catholic
missionary did notable work in the Field of opening
some elementary schools and some orphanage.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-II)
questions.questionText:
17. Who helped Monier Williams in preparation of
his Sanskrit English Dictionary before leaving
for England to become a barrister?
questions.explanation:
Shyamji Krishna verma helped monier
Williams in preparation of his Sanskrit English
dictionary before leaving for England to become a
barrister- Shyamji Krishna verma completed High
school from munbai. He learnt Sanskrit in traditional
school. he was well versed in both Sanskrit and English
In 1905 shyamji founded Indian home Rule society He
also started monthly magazine 'The Indian sociologist'

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-II)
questions.questionText:
18. The
Anandamatha
of
Bankim
Chandra
Chattopadhyay deals with :
questions.explanation:
The Anandamatha of Bankim Chandra
Chattopadhyay
to
deals
with
sanyasi
revolt.
Anandamatha was published in 1882. India's National
song 'Vande mataram' taken form Anandamatha
Britishers banned this novel.
* Bankim Chandra Chattoadhyay known as the
"Emperor of Bengali literature"

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-II)
questions.questionText:
19. G.D. Birla as a legislator in 1926-27 fought the
election on the ticket of which party?
questions.explanation:
G.D. Birla as a legislator in 1926-27 fought
the election on the ticket of nationalist party.
* G.D. Birla with other Industrialist proposed Bombay
plan for development of India in 1944.G.D. Birla was
also signatory of Bombay plan.
* Liberal party was founded in 1910.
* Swaraj party was founded in 1923 by C.R. Das &
Motilal Nehru.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-II)
questions.questionText:
20. Who started the 'Satya Prakash' in Gujarati in
1852 to advocate widow remarriage?
questions.explanation:
Karsandas Mulji started 'Satya prakash' in
Gujarati in 1820 to advocate widow remarriage. Later it
was merged with Rast Goftar news paper published
from Bombay. Karsandas come to prominence due to
Maharaja Libel Case in 1816 which was widely seen as
an attempt to reform religious practices.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-II)
questions.questionText:
21. The Cheros and Khairwars of Palamau rose
under whose leadership in the Revolt of 1857?
questions.explanation:
The Cheros and Khairwars of Palamou rose
under leadership of Pitambar Shahi in revolt of 1857. In
October 1857 500 people led by Pitambar attacked
Raghubar Dayal who had sided with british at chainpur.
Finally British suppressed revolt and Pitambar was
forced to flee.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-II)
questions.questionText: 22. Who wrote the book 'Hindutva'?
questions.explanation:
The book 'Hindutva' was written by V.D.
Savarkar. Savarkar also wrote as book titled "The
history of the war of Indian Independence" Savarkar
founded a secret society called Abhinav Bharat society.
Savarkar was convicted and sentenced to 50 years
imprisonment and transported to the cellular Jail in
Andaman and Nicobar islands.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-II)
questions.questionText:
23. Which of the following was not the part of the
Chauth income?
questions.explanation:
Nagabhaga was not the part of the Chauth
income. Chauth was a tax imposed by Marathas. It was
levied 25% on revenue. Total collected Chauth were
divided in 4 parts and went to various functionaries
Babti- 1/4 of Chauth goes to Chhatrapati
Nadgaunda- 3% of Chauth, Chhatrapati had discretionary
grant authority on this
Sahotra- 6% of Chauth granted to Pant Sachive
Two third of Chauth goes to Maratha Sardars who
collected the tax.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-II)
questions.questionText:
24. The new regiment of Indian National Army
(I.N.A.) raised at Taiping in Malaya in
September 1943 was called by the soldiers of
that Brigade as the ______
questions.explanation:
The new regiment of Indian National Army
(I.N.A) raised at Taiping in Malaya is September 1943
was called by the soldiers of that Brigades as the
Subhash.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-II)
questions.questionText:
25. Who is known as the Father of Land Settlement
in Northern India?
questions.explanation:
Robert Mertins Bird is known as the Father
of Land settlement in northern India. The Mahalwari
system was introduced by R.M. Bird. It was land tax
policy enforced in Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh,
Punjab and Delhi, In Mahalwari system revenue was
determined on Mahal'or whole village. Village headman
take responsibility of payment of revenue. Mahalwari
system was prevalent in 30% of British territory.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-II)
questions.questionText:
26. The first jute spinning mill in India was
established at Rishra in 1855 by whom?
questions.explanation:
The Acland mill was the first Jute mill
established in India. The mill was established in 1855
by George Acland and Bengali financier Babu
Bysumber Sen in Rishra Bengal presidency. After
partition in 1947 the Jute mills remained in India but 3/4
of Jute producing area went to Bangladesh.
* Central Research Institute for Jute and allied fibers is
located in West Bengal.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-II)
questions.questionText:
27. Which of the following was not the part of
Gandhi's constructive programme?
questions.explanation:
Inter Religion Marriage Association was not
the part of Gandhi's constructive programme.
constructive programmes are the social work Initiatives
of Mahatma Gandhi launched during inactive phase of
freedom struggle. Talimi sangh, Gram Udyog sangh,
Cow Protection Association were part of constructive
programme. By constructive programme Gandhi Ji
promoted Hindu Muslim unity and efforts for removal
of untouchability, constructive programme maintained

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-II)
questions.questionText:

extensively on Indian intellectual history
without learning any Indian lanaguage?
questions.explanation:
G.W.F. Hegel was German scholar who
wrote extensively on Indian intellectual history without
learning any Indian Language. Hegel was German
Idealist philosopher he wrote Critique on Bhagvad Gita.
His influence extends across the entire range of
contemporary philosophical topics, from metaphysical
issues in Epistemology to political philosophy, the
philosophy of history and the history of philosophy. He
got name by book the "Science of Logic."

questions.questionText:
30. Who among the following has inspired the
emergence of 'Psycho-history'?
questions.explanation:
Sigmund Freud has inspired the emergence of
'psycho-shistory'
The application of psychological model in historical
research known as psycho history. Psychohistory starts
from the Sigmund Freud's two psychohistorical
monographs 'Leonardo do Vinci and memory of his
childhood' and Masses-and monotheism. Although
Freud never used term psychohistory. Psycho history
term got prominence in 1960s.

Ranke?
questions.optionA:
He played a leading role in establishing
history as a respected discipline in the
universities
questions.optionB:
Established the notion that all sound history
must be based on primary sources
questions.optionC:
Established the notion that all sound history
must be based on rigorous methodology
questions.optionD: He was the father of the Romanticism
questions.explanation:
Leopold Von Ranke was 19th century
German Historian. He emphasized the importance of
research and analysis of primary sources to record
historical events properly. He established a notion that
all sound history must be based on rigorous method
logy. Ranke played a leading role in establishing history
as a respective discipline in the universities. He wrote a
famous book 'History of the Latin and Teutonic Nations'

Burns was first person to use Romanticism in

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-II)
questions.questionText:
39. Who asserted that "there is no middle state in
India".
questions.explanation:
Francois is Bernier asserted that "There is no
middle state in India". Bernier described Indian society
as consisting of undifferentiated masses of impoverished
people, subjugated by small minority of rich and
powerful ruling class. Between poorest of the poor and
the richest of rich- there was no social group hence
Bernier stated "There is no middle state in India".
* Francois bernier was French physician and traveller.
He lived in India twelve years from 1656 to 1668 He
wrote his account "Travels in the Mughal empire."

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-II)
questions.questionText:
40. Who said, "Film can open our minds to
another, more vivid and human, less literary
understanding of the past."
questions.explanation:
Pierre sorlin said "Film can open our minds
to another more vivid and human less literary
understanding of the past." Pierre Sorlin was French
historian. He believed in close relation between
Cinematic representation and historical narratives. He
produced major contribution on the representation of
Russian Revolution and on French popular cinema. He
stated that during teaching of History he used cinema as
additional sources which allowed knowing people by
sight instead of merely relying on textual portraits and
in some cases to witness the course of events

capital inscription and in the Chandravali stone
inscription of the Kadamba Mayurasarman, The Jaina
work 'Kalakacharya- Kathanaka states that saka kings
were called Sahi.' The Harivamsa Purana mentions that
sakas shaved one half of their heads. Sakas were
divided in 5 branches one in Afghanistan, second in
Punjab, third in Mathura, fourth in western India Fifth
in upper Deccan.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-II)
questions.questionText:
58. Which of these are correct :

(A) The first newspaper in India, the 'Bengal
Gazette' was also known by the name
'Calcutta General Advertiser'.

(B) Bengal Gazette's criticism of the Government
officials and attack on the Governor General
led to seizure of its press.

(C) The Censorship of the Press Act was
introduced in 1809 A.D.

(D) The Licensing Regulations of 1823 was
introduced by John Adams, as Acting
Governor-General.

(E) The Press Act (1835) repealed the obnoxious
Ordinance of 1823.

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below :
questions.optionC: A, B, C and E only
questions.optionD: A, B, D and E only
questions.explanation:
The first newspaper of India the Bengal
Gazette (also known as Calcutta General Adventiers)
was published in 1780 by James Augustus Hickey.
Bengal Gazette's criticism of the government officials
and attack on the governor general led to seizure of its
press Licensing Regulations 1823 was introduced by
John Adams as acting governor general. It made
mandatory license to open a press. The press act 1835
repealed obnoxious ordinance of 1823.
* The censorship of press Act was intruded in 1799 by
Lord Wellesley

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-II)
questions.questionText:
59. Which of the following are correct:

(A) In the Svetasvatara Upanishad, Siva figure as
the God superior to the Vedic pantheon.

(B) Siva is classed among minor gods, both in
Āpastamba Gṛihya Sūtra and Kauṭilya's
Arthasastra.

(C) A four-armed figure of the god Vishnu-
Vasudeva, with chakra in the upper left hand,
is found on the coins of the Panchala King
Vishnumitra.

(D) In the Anguttara Nikaya reference is made of
Ajivikas who shifted their center of activities
to the Pundra country.

(E) Vinayaka, a synonym of Ganesa, occurs in
the Atharvasiras Upanishad.

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below :
questions.optionC: A, C, D and E only
questions.optionD: A, B, C and E only
questions.explanation:
Statement A, B, C and E are correct,
Statement (D) is not correct that Anguttar Nikaya
mentioned Ajivikas shifted their center of activity to the
Pundra country.
Ashokavadan mentions that Ashoka issued an order to
kill all the Ajivikas in Pundra country.
Anguttara Nikaya mentioned sixteen Mahajanapadas
and life history of Buddha.
* Ajivika Sect was founded by Makhali Gosala in 5th
century BCE.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-II)
questions.questionText:
60. Which of these are correct :

(A) Forest Act of 1865 merely empowered the
state to assert control over forest resources
that it immediately required while still
Acknowledging a need to respect the existing
rights of forest users.

(B) The Forest Act of 1878 established the basic
categories of 'Reserved' and 'Protected'
forests.

(C) Under the Forest Act of 1878, reserve forests
were made an exclusive state monopoly.

(D) The Forest Act of 1878, allowed people slash
and burn shifting agriculure in Reserved
forests.

(E) The Forests Act of 1878, allowed grazing in
Reserve forests.

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below :
questions.optionC: A, B, C and D only
questions.optionD: A, B, C and E only
questions.explanation:
The Indian Forest Act was first enacted in
1865 which merely empowered the state to assert
control over forest resources, The forest Act 1878
divided forest into three categories (i) Reserved forest
(ii) protected forest (iii) village forest
Reserved forest-best forests, villagers could not take
anything from these forests over for their own use. The
basic aim was to remove local rights in the reserved
forest and keep them exclusively as government
reserves.
Protected forests were those forests areas where it was
not possible to reduce local use while village forests
were to be assigned to fulfill subsistence need.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-II)
questions.questionText:
61. Which of these are correct regarding Quit
India Movement, 1942.

(A) In Contai, the swaraj panchayat was started in
November, 1942.

(B) Tamralipta Jatiya Sarkar has a women's corps
known as Bhagini Sena.

(C) The parallel government established at
Tamluk started the mouthpiece, 'Biplabi'.

(D) In Talchar, during the 'Quit India movement'
"Chasi-mulia raj" was established.

(E) The "Chasi-mulia raj" in Tamluk was a
parallel government of feudal landlords.

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below :
questions.optionC: A, B, C and D only
questions.optionD: A, C, D and E only
questions.explanation:
The Quit India movement proposal passed in
8 August 1942 in Gawalia tank Bombay. During Quit
India movement parallel governments were established
in several places of India. In Contain, (West Bengal)
Swaraj Panchayat was started in November 1942
Tamluk (Bengal) parallel government started the mouth
piece 'Biplabi'.
In Talchar chasi mulia raj was established.
In Balia parallel government established under Chittu
Pandey. Satara was longest living parallel government.

questions.questionText:

(A) The cave temple Sittannavasal in Pudukottai
contains some fine paintings of the time of
the Pallava king Mahendravarman.

(B) A copper image of Buddha was erected at
Bodh-Gaya in Bihar at the close of 6th
century.

(C) The Buddha figures in general can be
classified under three main types, viz.
sthanaka (standing), asana (seated) and
sayana (recumbent).

(D) In some sculptures from Gandhara, Mathura
and Sarnath, the hair on Buddha's head is
shown as curled, turning from right to left.

(E) In the Gandhara style, Buddha is usually
shown with his right hand raised in abhaya
mudra.

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below :
questions.optionA: A, C, D and E only
questions.explanation:
Statement A, C and E are correct statement
(B) is not correct because copper image of Buddha
found from Nalanda and Sultanganj (in Bhagalpur
district) these images belong to 7th century. Statement
(D) is not correct because some sculptures from
Gandhara, Mathura and Sarnath, the hair on Buddha's
head is shown as curled with linear strokes over the
head.

questions.questionText:
63. Which of these are correct :

(A) Peshwa Baji Rao II died at Bithur.

(B) In 1803, Treaty of Surji Arjangaon was
conducted between the Holkars and the
British.

(C) Treaty of Saugauli was signed between the
English and the Raja of Nepal.

(D) Ahilya Bai Holkar died in 1793.

(E) Mahadji Sindhia concluded a treaty of
friendship with Sikh chiefs in May 1785.

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below :
questions.optionB: A, B, C and D only
questions.explanation:
Statement (A) (C) and (E) are correct.
Statement (B) is not correct because Treaty of surji
Arjangaon (1803) was concluded between the Scindhia
and the British not with Holkars. Treaty of Rajpur Ghat
(1804) concluded with Holkars.
Statement (D) is not correct because Ahilyabai Holkar
died in 1795 not in 1793. Ahilya Bai Holkar ruled 30
years. She established Maheswar (M.P.) as the seat of
Holkar dynasty.

questions.questionText:
64. Which of these are correct :

(A) Jinnah acted as Dadabhai's Secretary at the
Calcutta Congress of 1906.

(B) Elections were held in British India in
November 1923 for the central legislative
assembly.

(C) Jinnah focused on reviving the Muslim
League at its Lahore Session in 1923.

(D) After 1923, Jinnah wanted to continue co-
operation with Congress on the same terms of
the Lucknow Pact.

(E) The Hindu Mahasabha members like Madan
Mohan Malviya, B.S. Moonje and Lajpat Rai
rejected any reconciliation with the Muslim
Leauge.

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below :
questions.optionC: A, B, C and D only
questions.optionD: A, B, C and E only
questions.explanation:
M.A. Jinnah born in 1876 in Karachi. In 1906
he acted as Dadabhai's secretary at the Calcutta
congress of 1906. In 1916 Jinnah was elected as
president of Muslim league. In 1916 Lucknow pact was
signed between Congress and Muslim league. Elections
were held in British India in November 1923 for central
legislative assembly. Jinnah focused on reviving muslim
league at its Lahore session in 1923. Hindu Mahasabha
members like B.S. Moonje and Lajpat Rai rejected any
reconciliation with Muslim league. In reconciliation
with Muslim league. Lahore session of Muslim league
demanded Pakistan in 1940.

early. Like Sankara, he taught in many parts of India, and

believed that the spirit no less than matter must
be accepted as real, for it is impossible to
conceive of one quite independently of the
other.

Reason R : Love and Sivam are not different
categories of experience. Love culminates into
Sivam and rests in that beatific condition. In
the light of the above statement, choose the
correct answer from the options given below:
questions.optionA:
Both A and R are true and R is the correct
explanation of A.
questions.optionB:
Both A and R are true and R is not the correct
explanation of A.
questions.optionC: A is true but R is false.
questions.optionD: A is false but R is true.
questions.explanation:
Assertion (A) is correct that Tirumular, the
author of work called Tirumandiram on Saiva
Siddhanta, believed that the spirit no less than matter
must be accepted as real, for it is impossible to conceive
of one quite independently to the other
Reason(R) is also correct that love and sivam are not
different categories of experience. Love culminates into
sivam and rests in beatific condition.
Tirumular was a Tamil shaivite mystic and writer

favour.

D. Hood Stone

E. Alignment

given below :
questions.optionD: A, B, C, D and E
questions.explanation:
A megalith is a large stone that has been used
to construct a prehistoric structure or monument, either
alone or together with other stones, menhir, cairn circle,
Dolmenoid cist, Hood stone and alignment are forms of
megalithic structures.

memory of death of person in megalithic period.
* Cairn Circle- Prehistoric stone row which is a liner
arrangement of parallel megalithic standing stones.
* Dolmenoid Cist- It is burial chamber made of stone
both for sides and cap

of their buildings white because of this gradually this
area began to be known as "White town"
Hence Statement A, B,C and D are correct.

pestilence.

British goods when Elgin, the Viceroy
imposed an excise duty on Indian mill-
made cloth.

with spreading hatred disaffection against
the British Government.

rigorous imprisonment for 18 months.

freedom activist and belong to extremist sect. Tilak
adviced peasants in Maharashtra to withhold payment
of land revenues when their crop failed owing to
Drought or famine or pestilence. He is earliest
profounder of Swadeshi and Boycott. In 1896 Tilak

In 1897 Tilak arrested and charged with spreading

during the southern movement of Sun.

B. The groom takes the bride around the fire
(Agniparinaya).

C. The marriage rite starts with Kanyadana
(giving away the daughter).

D. According to most text, the marraige rite
end with the Saptapadi.

E. The
dhruvarundhatidarshana
was
a
marraige rite practice at the groom's house.

Choose the most appropriate answer from the
options given below :
questions.optionA: A, B, C and D only
questions.optionD: B, C, D and E only
questions.explanation:
Grihya Sutra describe the ceremonies
(samskaras) that mark each stage of an individual's life
from conception to the final death rites. According to
Grihya sutra following statement are true about
marriage ceremony.
(i) The groom takes the bride around the fire
(Agniparinaya)
(ii) According to the most texts, the marriage rite ends
with Saptapadi.
(iii) Dhruvaarundhatidarshana was a marriage rite
practice at the groom's house. so option(c) is correct
answer.

dominance in Bengal during Jahangir's

lost Quandhar to the Safavids in 1649.

Chittore.

control on Bengal and renamed Dacca as Jahangir
Nagar.

mughal emperor. Kumaon also accepted suzerainty of
Shahjahan.

Shahjahan's commandar Kasim khan seized Hooghly
from Portuguese.
Hence option D is correct answer.

supplying traditionally fixed quantities of
their products to peasant families in return
shares in the harvest.

B. A novel. 'Ganadevta' by Tarashankar
Bandopadhyay described village life in an
interior district of West Bengal in the
1920s and 1930s.

C. 'Ganadevta' portrayed the decline of the
Jajmani system.

D. Jajmani system only limited to religious
services given by brahmins to their J
ajmanis.

E. Jajmani system was part of the urban life
during the British colonial period.

given below :
questions.optionC: A, B, C and D only
questions.optionD: A, B, C and E only
questions.explanation:
Jajmani system was originated in medieval
India and continued till modern period. Jajmani system
was based on the village artisans supplying traditionally
fixed quantities of their products to peasants families in
return from shares in the harvest. A novel 'Ganadevta'
by Tarashankar Banddopadhyay describes village life in
an interior district of west Bengal in the 1920's and
1930's. 'Ganadevata' partrayed the decline of Jajmani
System.
So option (b) is correct answer.

regarding Painted Grey Ware (PGW)?

(in Bareilly district) in the 1940s.

B. It also been found at sites of Thapli and
Purola in the coastal region of Orissa.

C. Makkhan Lal's study of Kanpur district
(Uttar Pradesh) in 1980's brought to lights
the PGW sites and their settlement
patterns.

D. Nagda represents a fairly evolved proto-
urban or semi-urban stage of the PGW.

E. Alamgirpur, Kampil, Noh, Bhagwanpur
and Hastinapur have the evidence of the
PGW Material culture.

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below :
questions.optionB: A, B, C and D only
questions.optionD: B, C, D and E only
questions.explanation:
Painted Grey ware culture is an iron age
Indo-Aryan culture of western Gangetic plain and
Ghagger Hakra valley in Indian subcontinent dated
between 1200-500 BCE.
First PGW site was identified at Ahichchhatra (in
Bareilly district) in the 1940s.
Makkhan lal's study of Kanpur district (Uttar prdesh) in
1980s brought to light the PGW sites and their
settlement patterns.
Alamgirpur, Kampil Noh, Bhagwanpur and Hastinapur
have the evidence of PGW material culture.

questions.questionText: 80. What is the meaning of the term 'monopsony'?
questions.optionA:
It is a form of market with many sellers but
only one buyer, who is in a position to dictate
terms to the sellers
questions.optionB:
It is a form of market with one seller, but
many buyers and buyer have no choice.
questions.optionC:
It is a form of market where there are many
sellers and many buyers and both have
multiple choices.
questions.optionD:
It is a market in which there are two sellers
and many buyers having limited choices.
questions.explanation:
The term Monopsony defines A form of
market with many sellers but only one buyer, who is in
a position to dictate terms to the sellers.
* Monopoly is a form of market with one seller but
many buyers and buyer have no choice.
* Perfect competition is form of market where there are
many sellers and many buyers and both have multiple
choice.
* Duopoly It is a market in which there are two sellers
and many buyers having limited choices.

Communists continued their United Front
Policy against all types of imperialism.

B. When Hitler attacked the Soviet Union,
Communists in India staged a right-about
turn, and relabelled the war as a 'people's
war'.

support and even acted as British 'spies' in
suppressing the popular revolt of 1942.

D. Government
of
India
rewarded
the
Communist Party of India (CPI) by
declaring it as a legal organization in 1942.

E. It clearly demonstrated that the CPI's
policy decisions were dictated by outside
and international wire pullers.

options given below:
questions.optionB: A, B, C and D only

communist continued their united Front policy against
all type of imperialism.
When Hitler attacked the Soviet union, communists in
India staged a right-about turn and relabbelled the war
as people's war. Communists in India extended all
possible support even acted as british 'spies' in
suppressing the popular revolt of 1942. Government of
India rewarded the communist party of India declaring a
legal organisation in 1942. But it does not demonstrated
that the CPI's policy decisions were dictated by outside
and international wire puller.
Hence A, B, C and D are Correct Statement.

Boustrephedon is a unique style of writing
charactered by it's bi-directional Nature, Where text
alternates between left to right and right to left in a Zig-

the plowing path of an OX.

questions.questionText:
30. Given below are two statements:

Statement I : The root cause of the Vellore
mutiny was the brazen English attempt to
convert the Indian soldiers to Christianity
under the guise of military discipline.

Statement II : The sepoys were also ordered to
change their traditional turbans for the kind of
head-dress adopted by Indian converts to
Christianity

In the light of the above statements, choose the
most appropriate answer from the options
given below :
questions.optionA: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.optionB:
Both Statement I and Statement II are
incorrect
questions.optionC:
Statement I is correct but Statement II is
incorrect
questions.optionD:
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is
correct
questions.explanation:
Both Statement I and II are correct.
Vellore mutiny took place on 10 July 1806. This was
first major revolt of sepoys before 1857. Cause of the
Vellore mutiny was English disregard to the religious
sensitivities of Hindu and Muslim Indian sepoys. Sir
John Craddock, commander in chief of Madras army
had issued orders prohibiting soldiers from wearing
religious marks on their foreheads and also to trim
moustache's and shave off their beards. This offended
both Hindus and Muslims. They were asked to wear
round hats instead of traditional turban.

Statement II : The temple of Kailash was built
by cutting away more than fifty million tonnes
of rock from the sloping hill in the region.

In the light of the above statements, choose the
most appropriate answer from the options
given below :
questions.optionA: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
questions.optionB: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.optionC: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
questions.optionD: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.explanation:
Both Statement I and II are correct
The Kailash temple Ellora is an unparalleled monument
in terms of its artistry and craftsmanship of Indian rock
cut architecture. The temple of Kailash was built by
cutting away more than fifty million tonnes of rock
from the sloping hill in the region. It was built by single
block of excavated stone. It was perhaps built by
Rashtrakuta king Krishna I.
This temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2023 (16.06.2023, Shift-II)
questions.questionText: 56. What does the word Mashrut refer to
questions.optionD: Only reserved for the royal Princes
questions.explanation:

Rank.

service and were independent of rank were called
Inam jagir.
* Watan Jagir- Jagirs which were assigned to

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2023 (16.06.2023, Shift-II)
questions.questionText:

under the Widow Remarriage Act (1856) was
celebrated at the residence of _________.
questions.explanation:
On 7 December 1856 Ishwar chandra
Vidyasagar married of the first widow, much to digust
and opposition of Hindu conservation.
The Widow Kalimati the daughter of Brahmananda
Mukherjee was married to Shrishchandra Vidyaratna
at the house of Raj Krishna in Calcutta.

July 1856. It was drafted by Lord Dalhousie and
passed by Lord Canning.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2023 (16.06.2023, Shift-II)
questions.questionText:
58. The Nayaks who were local military chiefs
were recognized as key political figures in the
Vijayanagara state.

A. The Nayaks possessed land rights granted
to them by the Vijayanagara king.

B. The Nayaks were the owners of all lands in
the empire.

C. The Nayaks have completely dependent on
the decisions of the kings of Vijayanagara
until
1565,
later
they
became
semi
independent.

D. The Nayaks also worked as feudatories
with conditional military tenure as 75% of
the Vijayanagara empire was under amaram.

E. The Nayaks also colluded with the Afaqi
and Dakhini nobles of the Bahmani
kingdom.

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below :
questions.explanation:
Nayakar System was prevalent in Vijaynagar
empire, Nayakas were military chiefs of Vijayanagar
kings. Vijayanagar king assign them land rights. The
Nayakas were the owners of all lands in the empire.
Nayakas have completely dependent on the decision of
the kings of Vijayanagar until 1565, later they became
semi independent. The Nayaks also worked as
feudatories with conditional military tenure as 75% of
Vijayanagar empire was under Amaran. Nayakas never
colluded with Afaqi and Dakhini Nobles of the
Bahmani Kingdom.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2023 (16.06.2023, Shift-II)
questions.questionText:

Chronological order

A. Battle of Arbela

B. Battle of Pallalur

C. Battle of Tarain

D. Battle of Takkolam

E. Battle of Hydaspes

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2023 (16.06.2023, Shift-II)
questions.questionText:
60. Who among the following was a Dutch traveler
to Agra in the 17th Century?
questions.explanation:
Francisco Pelsaert was a Dutch merchant
who worked for the Dutch East India company. He
sailed to India in 1618, where he was posted as a junior
merchant, spending seven years in Agra he became
senior merchant after a brief return to the united
province in 1628, he departed for Java.
Francisco Pelsaert mentioned production of Indigo in
Bayana.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2023 (16.06.2023, Shift-II)
questions.questionText:
61. Given below are two statements :

Statement I : Kasturba Gandhi died in
February 1944 in the Aga Khan palace.

Statement II: Mahatma Gandhi pleaded guilty
to charge of sedition for writing three articles
in young India-the articles were 'Tampering
with Loyalty' 'A puzzle and its solution' and
'Shaking the Manes'

In the light of the above statements, choose the

given below:

Statement I is true that Kasturba Gandhi died
