questions.questionText:
14. Which of the following is not associated with
the Stupa?
questions.optionA:
It originated as a simple semi-rectangular
mound of earth.
questions.optionB:
Gradually, it evolved into a more complex
structure, balancing round and square shapes.
questions.optionC:
It also consisted of 'harmika' a balcony like
structure that represented the abode of gods.
questions.optionD:
Arising from the harmika was a mast called
the yashti.
questions.explanation:
The Stupa (Sanskrit meaning: mound)
originated from a hemispherical mound of earth, which
was later called the Anda (egg). Gradually, its structure
became more complex, incorporating a balance of
several square and circular shapes. Above the Anda was
a Harmika. This balcony-like structure symbolized the
abode of the Gods. A mast emerged from the Harmika,
called the Yashti, on which an umbrella (Chattri) was
often placed.

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (June 2024) Nirsat
questions.questionText:
15. What were the unfortified trading outposts
which also served as strategic bases for the
naval fleet of Portuguese known as?
questions.explanation:
Unfortified trading posts that served as
strategic bases for the Portuguese naval fleet were
called Feitorias.
Portuguese Feitorias were mostly fortified trading posts
situated in coastal areas, built to centralize and
dominate local trade of products with the Portuguese
Empire. They simultaneously served as a market-
warehouse and as an aid for customs. The first
Portuguese Feitoria overseas was established by Henry
the Navigator on Arghin Island off the coast of
Mauritania in 1445 CE.

questions.questionText: 16. Who were the 'Satavahanas'?
questions.explanation:
In the first century BCE, two powers gained
prominence in the south of the Vindhya Mountains: the
Satavahanas of the Upper Deccan and the Chedis of
Kalinga. The power of the Chedis was short-lived, but
the Satavahana power continuously flourished for three
centuries, and their authority continued in some form
for four and a half centuries. The entire Dakshinapatha
(Deccan) was included under the Satavahana Empire.
The Satavahana emperors not only protected their
independence against foreigners but also paved the way
for the material and cultural progress of their subjects
by encouraging literature, art, trade, and commerce.

questions.questionText:
18. King Kharavela of Kalinga was an ardent
follower of which religion?
questions.explanation:
The founder of the Chedi dynasty of Kalinga
was a person named Mahameghavahana. The most
powerful king of this dynasty was Kharavela. Kharavela
was a follower of Jainism; he provided patronage to
Jain ascetics. In the thirteenth year of his reign, he had
cave-monasteries (Guha-Viharas) carved out of the
Udayagiri and Khandagiri hills near Bhubaneswar for
the residence of Jain monks.

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (June 2024) Nirsat
questions.questionText:
19. Which Act separated Burma from India and
suggested the creation of two new provinces of
Sind and Orissa?
questions.explanation:
The 1919 reforms could not satisfy the Indian
citizens, and after the Gandhi-Irwin Pact and the Round
Table Conferences, the British government issued a
White Paper in February 1935, which mentioned new
reforms. Under this scheme of reforms, the Government
of India Act, 1935, was passed in August 1935.
Through this law, Burma and Aden were separated from
the administration of India, two new provinces in the
form of Sindh and Orissa were created, and the North-
West Frontier Province was placed under two
Governors. A Federal Court and a Central Bank (which
came to be known as the Reserve Bank of India) were
established under the Government of India Act, 1935.

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (June 2024) Nirsat
questions.questionText: 20. What was 'Anand Karaj' related to?
questions.explanation:
The Sikh wedding, known as 'Anand Karaj,'
which means 'Blissful Union,' was initiated by the third
Guru of Sikhism, Guru Amar Das. The Sikh wedding
ceremony is held in the presence of the Guru Granth
Sahib. Anand Karaj is usually held in a Gurdwara,
which is the central place of worship for Sikhs.

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (June 2024) Nirsat
questions.questionText:
21. How many grades, Akbar had created in his
Mansabdari System?
questions.explanation:
Akbar created 66 ranks in his Mansabdari
System. The word 'Mansab' means rank or position, and
a 'Mansabdar' was an officer who held a rank or
position in the Imperial army. Akbar's Mansabdari
system was based on the decimal system. Abul Fazl
mentions 66 ranks (mansabs), but in practice, only 33
mansabs are mentioned in the Ain-i-Akbari. This
suggests that some ranks were not granted, and to
simplify the system, some ranks were abolished, which
reduced the number of ranks in practice. These mansabs
were granted from ten up to twelve thousand.

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (June 2024) Nirsat
questions.questionText: 22. What is the meaning of term 'Srenis'?
questions.explanation:
The role of guilds (Shreni) was extremely
important in the economic life of ancient India. The
organization of different artisans was called a Shreni. A
Shreni was an institution of people engaged in the same
type of occupation or industry. The control of trade was
essentially in their hands. They conducted both internal
and external trade.

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (June 2024) Nirsat
questions.questionText:
23. Which of the following works belongs to second
Sangam?
questions.explanation:
The composition related to the Second
Sangam is Tolkappiyam. The systematic history of
South India is known through Sangam Literature. The
word 'Sangam' means a council or assembly where
Tamil poets and scholars gathered and presented their
compositions before the Sangam. A total of three
Sangams were organized under the patronage of the
Pandya kings:
1. First Sangam: Held in Madura. It was presided over
by Agastya Rishi. The texts compiled by this
Sangam
included
Akattiyam,
Paripadal,
and
Mudunarai.
2. Second Sangam: Held in Kapatapuram (Alavai). It
was presided over by Agastya. The only surviving
text compiled by this Sangam is 'Tolkappiyam', a
Tamil grammar text composed by Tolkappiyar.
3. Third Sangam: Held in the Pandya capital, Madura.
The compositions of this Sangam included
Kuruntokai, Parinupattu, and Pari-padal.

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (June 2024) Nirsat
questions.questionText:
24. The technique of tin-coating in India was
introduced by the :
questions.explanation:
The technique of tin-plating (tinning) in India
was introduced by the Turks. A discovery of the Turks
in Indian metallurgy was the application of tin (kalai)
on copper vessels. The tin-platers were called
'Kalaigars'. Tin (Rangar) is a highly malleable and
ductile metal, and its plating on metal vessels provides
them protection from rust and chemical poisoning.
Tinning is mentioned in Abul Fazl's 'Ain-i-Akbari'.

questions.questionText:
34. Arrange
the
following
events
in
the
chronological order :

A. Establishment of the Sultanates of Gujarat
and Malwa.

B. Establishment of the Gajapati Kingdom of
Orissa.

C. Establishment of the Bahmani Kingdom

D. Victory of Portuguese over Goa.

E. Establishment of the Ahom Kingdom of
Assam.

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below :
questions.explanation:
The systematic chronological order of the
events is as follows :
(i) Ahom Kingdom a Late Medieval kingdom
established in the Brahmaputra Valley of Assam in
1228 CE. The foundation of the Ahom Kingdom
was laid by the first Ahom king, Chaolung Sukapha.
(ii) Bahmani Kingdom Established in 1347 CE by
Alauddin Bahman Shah (original name Hasan and
nickname Hasan Gangu).
(iii) Zafar Khan made his son Tatar Khan the Sultan of
Gujarat by giving him the title of Nasiruddin in
1401 CE. The real founder of the Gujarat state is
considered to be Ahmad Shah I (1411-1442 CE). In
1401 CE, Dilawar declared himself the independent
ruler of Malwa but did not adopt the title of Sultan.
Dilawar's son Alp Khan adopted the title of Hoshang
Shah and declared himself Sultan in 1406 CE.
(iv) Gajapati
Dynasty
of
Odisha:
Founded
by
Kapilendra in 1434 CE.
(v) Portuguese Conquest of Goa: Portuguese Governor
Afonso de Albuquerque seized Goa from the Adil
Shahi ruler in 1510 CE.
Note: None of the options matched the correct sequence.

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (June 2024) Nirsat

35. Arrange in the chronological order :

A. Conquest of Goa by the Portuguese

B. Establishment of Bahamani Kingdom

C. Establishment of the Mughal empire by
Babur

D. Establishment of the Delhi Sultanate

E. Emergence of the Sultanate of Golcondo

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below :
questions.explanation:
The systematic chronological order is as
follows:
(i) Delhi Sultanate: Started in 1206 CE by Qutb-ud-
din Aibak, the ruler of the Mamluk dynasty.
(ii) Bahmani Kingdom: Established by Alauddin
Bahman Shah in 1347 CE.
(iii) Portuguese Conquest of Goa: The Portuguese took
control of Goa in 1510 CE.
(iv) Rise of Golconda Sultanate: Emerged under the
leadership of Qutb Shah between 1512–1518 CE,
as part of the disintegration of the Bahmani
Kingdom.
(v) Mughal Empire: Established by Babur on April 21,
1526 CE, by defeating Ibrahim Lodi in the battle
of Panipat. Ibrahim Lodi attained martyrdom on
the battlefield of Panipat, which was the first
instance of a Delhi Sultanate ruler dying in battle.

questions.explanation:

central and provincial governments in protest
against the Viceroy's decision to include India in
World War II. The Muslim League decided to
observe 'Deliverance Day' on December 22, 1939,
to celebrate the resignations.
(ii) Pakistan Resolution was presented by the Muslim
League on March 22, 1940, and adopted on March
23, 1940. It is also known as the Lahore
Resolution. The League's three-day session was
held in Lahore from March 22–24, 1940.
(iii) Rabindranath Tagore (Gurudev) was born on May
7, 1861, and passed away in 1941 CE. He was a
distinguished figure as a poet, litterateur, and
philosopher.
(iv) Subhas Chandra Bose proclaimed the Provisional
Government of Free India in Singapore.
(v) Naval mutiny by members of the Royal Indian
Navy in Bombay.

questions.questionText: 49. Who were known as 'Vindhya Sakti'?
questions.explanation:
The Vakataka Dynasty was founded in the
middle of the 3rd century CE by Vindhyashakti of the
Vishnuvriddha Gotra. Their ancestors were local rulers
of Berar under the Satavahanas. After the Satavahanas,
Vindhyashakti declared his independence. The empire
extended north of the Vindhya Mountains up to Eastern
Malwa. During the time of Vindhyashakti's son,
Pravarsena I (275–335 CE), the Vakataka Empire
expanded from the Central Provinces and Bundelkhand
in the north to Northern Hyderabad in the south.

questions.explanation:

Nighantu (a collection of Vedic words). The objective
of Nirukta is to clarify the difficult vocabulary of the

53. Which of the following is not one of the salient
features of Indian Feudalism?
questions.explanation:
Not taking the surplus is not a characteristic
of Indian Feudalism.
The characteristics of Indian Feudalism include:
 The rise of a hierarchical structure of land
intermediaries.
 The prevalence of forced labor by peasants and
laborers.
 Curtailment of peasant land rights.
 Taking the surplus.

questions.questionText:
55. Which of the following are correct about the
dancing mentioned in the Bharata Natyasastra?

A. 13 postures of the head

B. 36 Postures of the eyes

C. 09 postures of the neck

D. 37 postures of the hand

E. 20 postures of the body

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below :
questions.optionD: A, B, C and D Only
questions.explanation:
Bharata Muni's Natyashastra describes 13
gestures of the head, 36 glances/movements of the eyes,
09 movements of the neck, and 37 gestures of the hand.
The Natyashastra analyzes every aspect related to
theatrical performances. The concept of Abhinaya
(acting) is explained in detail in this treatise. Abhinaya
is the art by which an artist conveys a dramatic feeling
to the audience through their speech, emotions, or
various movements of the body.

following?

A. Mitra Mela

B. The Indian War of Independence, 1857

C. India House

D. Fergusson College

questions.optionC: A, B, C, D and E
questions.optionD: A, B, C and E Only
questions.explanation:
V.D. Savarkar was associated with the
following:
 V. D. Savarkar, along with Gatos Savarkar, founded
the organization 'Mitra Mela' in Nashik in 1899 CE.
Mitra Mela later transformed into 'Abhinav Bharat'
in 1904 CE.
 Shyamji Krishna Varma, a resident of the Kathiawar
state of Gujarat, graduated as a barrister from
Cambridge University, London. In 1905, he formed
the 'India Home Rule Society' (also called India
House) in London. V.D. Savarkar took advantage of
Krishna Varma's fellowship and went to London in
1906,
where
he
contributed
to
the
Indian
independence struggle in various ways.

1857', which was published in 1909.
 He graduated from Fergusson College, Poona.
Note : The Madras Native Association (MNA) was
established in Madras (present-day Chennai) in 1852. It
was the first Indian political association formed in the
Madras Presidency. The MNA was not associated with
V.D. Savarkar.

59. Which out of the following are correct?

A. Wilhelm Dilthey stated "what man is, only
history tells.

B. James Thurber stated, "It is better to
know some of the question than all of the
answers".

C. Cicero stated, "Rewriting is the essence of
writing well : It's where the game is won or
lost".

D. Henry Adams stated, "History does not
repeat itself. The historians repeat each
other."

E. Colling wood stated, "If History teaches us
any lesson at all, it is that there are no
historical lessons."

questions.optionC: A, B, D and E Only

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (June 2024) Nirsat
questions.questionText:
60. Which of the following is not associated with
the main tasks of spies under the Mauryan
administration?
questions.optionA: Keeping an eye over the ministers.
questions.optionC: Knowing the secret of foreign rulers.
questions.optionD:
Collecting no impressions regarding the
feelings of citizens.
questions.explanation:
The Espionage Department held an important
position
in
the
Mauryan
administration.
This
department was placed under a separate Amatya
(Minister) called the Mahamatya-Pasarpa. Spies are
referred to as 'Gūḍhapurusha' (secret men) in the
Arthashastra. There were two types of spies: Samstha
(static spies) and Sanchara (wandering spies). The main
duty of the spies was to keep an eye on Amatyas,
Ministers, royal employees (government officials), and
citizens (Paur Janapadas), as well as to gather all
information about neighboring states (foreign rulers).
The spies of the Mauryan period also gathered
information about the feelings of the citizens and
conveyed it to the King.

questions.questionText: 62. Which of the following is not a Mahajanapada?
questions.explanation:
Before the rise of Gautama Buddha, the
entire North India was divided into 16 large states. This
is mentioned in the Buddhist text Anguttara Nikaya and
the Jain text Bhagavati Sutra. These include: Kashi,
Kosala, Anga, Magadha, Vajji, Malla, Chedi, Vatsa,
Kuru, Panchala, Matsya, Shurasena, Ashmaka, Avanti,
Gandhara, and Kamboja.
The names in the Bhagavati Sutra are slightly different:
Anga, Vanga or Banga, Magaha, Malaya, Malava,
Accha, Vaccha, Koccha, Patha, Ladha, Vajji, Moli,
Kashi, Kosala, Avadha, Sambhuttara, etc.
Note:
Thus,
Kuru,
Anga,
Vanga,
etc.,
were
Mahajanapadas, whereas Chera was a kingdom of the
Sangam period (South India).

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (June 2024) Nirsat

63. The queen Nayanika is associated with which
of the following dynasties?
questions.explanation:
After the death of Krishna, Shri Satakarni,
the son of Simuka, ascended the throne of the
Satavahana dynasty. He is famous as Satakarni I
because he was the first king in his dynasty to adopt the
title Satakarni. Satakarni I was the greatest among the
early Satavahana kings. He increased his influence by
marrying Nayanika (Naganika), the daughter of the
Maharathi Banakayira of the Angiya Kula. Important
information about the reign of Satakarni I is obtained
from Naganika's Naneghat Inscription.

questions.explanation:
The founder of the Mughal dynasty in India,
Emperor Zahiruddin Muhammad Babur, was himself a
scholar and a lover of learning. He wrote his
autobiography, Tuzuk-i-Baburi (Baburnama), in the
Turkic language. The Mughal ruler Jahangir, like his
grandfather Babur, also wrote his autobiography and
named it Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri (Jahangirnama). Jahangir
composed this work in the Persian language.
Note: Humayunama was written by Gulbadan Begum,
Akbarnama
was
written
by
Abul
Fazl,
and
Alamgirnama was written by Mirza Muhammad Kazim.
These works are not autobiographies but play an
important role in understanding the Mughal period.

out
of
the
following
were
the
administrative units?

A. Pathaka
B. Pattala

C. Vishaya
D. Vithi

E. Adaya

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below :
questions.optionA: A, B, C and E Only
questions.optionB: A, B, C and D Only
questions.optionD: B, C, D and E Only
questions.explanation:
Pathak (Pathaka), Pattala, Vishaya, and Vithi
were administrative units. Pathak (Pethaka) was a
district-level administrative unit during the Gupta
period.
The main purpose of the Pattala unit was revenue
collection. The district was called a 'Vishaya' during the
Gupta period, and its chief officer was the 'Vishayapati'.
Vithi was a village-level administrative unit during the
Gupta period.

68. Which of the following are the classes specified
by Meghasthenes?

A. Philosophers
B. Farmers

C. Soldiers
D. Artisans

E. Barbers

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below :
questions.optionC: A, D, C and D Only
questions.optionD: B, C, D and E Only
questions.explanation:
By the Mauryan period, the Varnashrama
system had acquired a definite basis. Varnas had
transformed into rigid castes based on birth. The
accounts of Greek writers provide information about the
extreme complexity of the caste system. The Greek
writer Megasthenes mentions seven classes in Indian
society: Philosophers, Farmers, Soldiers, Herdsmen/
Shepherds, Artisans, Supervisors /Inspectors, and
Councillors /Ministers. Megasthenes does not mention a
barber in his account.

questions.explanation:
Domingo Paes, describing the city of
Vijayanagara, said, "I am not writing the extent of
Vijayanagara here, because it cannot be seen completely
from one place, but I climbed a hill from where I could
see a large part of it. I could not see it entirely because it
is situated between many mountain ranges. From what I
saw there, it seemed to me as vast as Rome and
extremely beautiful to look at; it has many groves of
trees in the gardens of the dwellings, and many channels
of water running through it, and lakes in many places,
and near the king's palace, there were gardens of palm
trees and other fruit-bearing trees."

questions.questionText:
73. Holt Mackenzie was associated with which of
the following?
questions.explanation:
Holt Mackenzie was associated with the land
revenue settlement. An Englishman named Holt
Mackenzie prepared a new system (Mahalwari
Settlement) for the North-Western Provinces of the
Bengal Presidency (most of this area is now in Uttar
Pradesh), which was implemented in 1822. Mackenzie
believed that the village was an important social
institution in North Indian society and should be
preserved. On his orders, Collectors toured village after
village, inspected the land, measured the fields, and
recorded the customs of various groups. The estimated
revenue of each field in the village was added up to
calculate the revenue to be collected from each village
or group of villages (Mahal). This revenue was not
fixed permanently but kept open for revision from time
to time. The responsibility of collecting the revenue and
paying it to the Company was entrusted to the Village
Headman instead of the Zamindar. This system was
named the Mahalwari Settlement.

region?
questions.explanation:
The Roshaniya or Roshnai sect was founded
by the Afghani-origin Pir Bayazid Khan in the 16th
century. The region of this sect was the Northwest, i.e.,
present-day Afghanistan and Pakistan. It emerged
among the Pashtun tribes. The first founder of the
Qadiriyya branch was Sheikh Muhiyuddin Abdal Qadir
Gilani of Baghdad. The founder of the Suhrawardiyya
branch
was
Sheikh
Ziauddin
Abul
Jib.
The
Naqshbandiyya branch was founded by Khwaja
Bahauddin Naqshband in the 14th century.

economic, commercial, or material returns, was termed
the Drain of Wealth by Indian national leaders and
economists. The components of economic drain
(expatriation) included: interest on public debt taken
from abroad, purchase of stores in England, interest on
foreign capital investment, and earnings of foreign
banking, insurance, and shipping companies, etc.
Note : The components of the economic drain include
the dividend of the East India Company's shareholders,
and not the dividend of the British Crown's shareholders

questions.explanation:
The Chola Kingdom was the most powerful
among the states of the Sangam Age. It was situated
between the Penna and Southern Vellalar rivers. The
Chola ruler Karikala held an important position during
the Sangam period. He was a follower of Brahmanism
and provided patronage to this religion. We receive
highly exaggerated accounts of Karikala's achievements. It
is said that he conducted military campaigns up to the
Himalayas and conquered the Vajra, Magadha, and
Avanti kingdoms.

questions.explanation:
The first capital of the Haryanka dynasty
ruler Bimbisara was Girivraja (Rajagriha). The true
founder of the greatness of the Magadha Empire was
King Bimbisara (544–492 BCE). Bimbisara was a
friend and patron of Mahatma Buddha. It is known from
the Vinaya Pitaka that after meeting the Buddha, he
embraced Buddhism and gifted the Veluvana garden to
the Buddha and the Sangha. Bimbisara ruled for about
52 years. Eventually, his son, Ajatashatru (Kunika),
imprisoned him, where he was killed through severe
torture.

questions.explanation:

are inscribed on a fragmented rock located in Sopara,
Thane district, Maharashtra province. It is estimated
that all fourteen edicts must have existed here initially.
Ashoka's Major Rock Edicts have been obtained from
eight different places, which are: Shahbazgarhi
(Pakistan), Mansehra (Pakistan), Kalsi (Uttarakhand),
Girnar (Gujarat), Dhauli and Jaugada (Odisha),
Erragudi (Andhra Pradesh), and Sopara (Maharashtra).
Note: Minor Rock Edicts were found at Maski
(Karnataka), and Pillar Edicts were found at Meerut
(Uttar Pradesh), etc.

90. The statement below is attributed to which
historian?

St. Augustine looked at history from the point
of view of the early Christian; Tillamont from
that of a seventeenth century Frenchman;
Gibbon, from that of an eighteenth century
Englishman;
Mommsen
from that of a
nineteenth century German. There is no point
on asking which was the right point of view.
Each was the only one possible for the man
who adopted it:
questions.explanation:
The quote: "Saint Augustine saw history
from the point of view of early Christianity; Tillemont
like a Frenchman of the seventeenth century; Gibbon
like an Englishman of the eighteenth century;
Mommsen like a German of the nineteenth century. It is
meaningless to ask which point of view was correct.
Each point of view was the only possible one for the
man who adopted it." This statement belongs to the
famous philosophical historian and archaeologist Robin
George Collingwood. Seeing the importance of history,
Collingwood had also said, "We stand on a threshold
where history will be as important to the world as
natural science was between 1600–1900 CE."

Ramanuja was born around 1017 CE in a

name was Lakshmana. He received his early education

commentaries on the Brahma Sutras. Ramanuja

theory of Maya (illusion), stating that Moksha can be
attained by single-minded, trusting, and intense
devotion to God.

confluence of Vaishnava devotion and Upanishadic

questions.explanation:
The Arya Samaj worked for the reform of
Hindu religion and society in North India. The Arya

Bombay in 1875. Within a short time, its influence was
established over a large part of North India (Punjab,

greatest interest in it among the people outside its own

97. What does Suddhi means?
questions.optionA:
Suddhi means the reconversions of those
Hindus – millions in number – who had once
been willing or forcibly converted in to other
religions like Islam or Christianity, but were
now willing to come back to the fold of
Hinduism.
questions.optionB:
Suddhi means putting ceremonial water on
people to purify them.
questions.optionC:
Suddhi means doing rituals to purify people
from their impurities.
questions.optionD:
Suddhi means putting people in ceremonial
fire to purify them for their misdeeds.
questions.explanation:
Shuddhi refers to the reconversion of
Hindus— numbering in the millions—who had
voluntarily or forcibly converted to other religions like
Islam or Christianity, but who now wished to
voluntarily return to Hinduism. Swami Dayananda
Saraswati initiated the Shuddhi movement by inspiring
those who had converted to return to Hinduism. At that
time, Christian, Muslim, and Sikh preachers ridiculed
the social evils and false beliefs of Hinduism. Swami
Dayananda also pointed out flaws in their religions and
defeated ancient orthodox pandits and other religious
preachers through public debates. Consequently, a new
feeling of self-confidence, self-examination, and self-
purification (i.e., removing false traditions from
Hinduism) arose among the followers of Hinduism.
Although its external form sought to re-establish Vedic
traditions, the Arya Samaj essentially embraced modern
knowledge and logic.

98. How was Suddhi looked upon by Arya Samaj?

As a potent instrument for effecting that
religious, social and political unity of India
questions.optionB: As a tool to divide the people
questions.optionD: As a tactic to divert the attention of people
questions.explanation:
Shuddhi was viewed by the Arya Samaj as a
powerful tool for bringing about the religious, social,
and political unity of India. Swami Dayananda
Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj in Bombay in 1875,
with the main objective of purely re-establishing the
ancient Vedic religion. He vowed to eradicate the false
religious beliefs and social evils that had crept into
Hindu society over time. The Arya Samaj was
established in Lahore in 1877, after which its influence
grew significantly. His goal was to unite India
religiously, socially, and nationally. He wished for the
Aryan religion to be the common religion of the
country. He saw many faults in the contemporary Hindu
religion and society. In the religious sphere, he did not
accept idol worship, polytheism, incarnation theory,
animal sacrifice, Shraddha ceremonies, charms, mantras
and tantras, and false rituals. He considered the Vedas
to be divine knowledge and accepted literature up to the
Upanishadic period.

Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq's sudden death due to
lightning?
questions.explanation:
Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq, the founder of the
Tughlaq dynasty in the Delhi Sultanate, ruled from
1320 to 1325 AD. He adopted a policy of leniency in
contrast to Alauddin's harsh policies. Upon his return
from a successful campaign in Bengal, he was killed
when a wooden building constructed for a reception in
Tughlaqabad collapsed. However, historian Barani
attributes his death to lightning.

questions.questionText:
3.
Which of the following statements are correct?

(A) The basic unit of South Indian village life
in the early medieval period was the ur

(B) The
ur
was
associated
with
village
assemblies as well as the village

(C) The ur was a non-brahmadeya village

(D) Corporate bodies such as the nadu, sabha,
and
nagaram
did
not
perform
the
functions
of
assessing
and
collecting
revenue

Select the correct answer from the options
given below.
questions.explanation:
Chola inscriptions broadly mention three
types of village assemblies: the ur, the sabha, and the
nagaram. The ur was a common type of village
assembly, forming the basic unit of village life. Ur
included both villages, puras, or towns. Ur was a non-
brahmadeya village because the brahmadeya village
council was called the assembly or Mahasabha. In the
Chola administration, below the balanadu was the nadu,
which was equivalent to a modern district, and its main
function was to manage land revenue.

questions.optionA:

to start or use a press.
questions.optionB:

request a new application.

(B) The emergency situation created by the Great
War of 1857 forced the British to reimpose
restrictions on the press. In addition to the
registration process then in effect in the
Metcalfe Act, Regulation Fifteen of 1857
redefined licensing restrictions.

(C) In March 1941, the Government of India
constituted a 'Press Inquiry Committee' and
entrusted it with the responsibility of
reviewing press laws.

(D) The Newspaper Act of 1908 empowered
magistrates to confiscate the printing presses
and other properties of newspapers found to
publish objectionable articles that incited
violence or murder.

Select the correct answer from the options
below:
questions.optionD:
Only (B), (C) and (D)

(c) Only (A), (C) and (D)

(d) Only (A), (B) and (D)
questions.explanation:
The Licensing Act of 1823 was enacted
during the reign of Governor General John Adams.
Under this Act, printers and publishers were required to
obtain a license to establish a press, while the Governor
General had the power to revoke the license or request a
new application. The Licensing Act was enacted to deal
with the Emergency Act arising from the 1857
rebellion. Under the 1908 Act, magistrates were
empowered to confiscate presses whose articles were
objectionable.
[Exam Date: 29.08.2024, Shift-I]

5.

Magadha?
questions.explanation:
In ancient India, the first dynasty of the
Magadha Empire was the Haryanka dynasty, founded
by Bimbisara and peaking during the reign of
Ajatashatru. After the Haryanka dynasty, Shaishunaga
established the Shaishunaga dynasty in Magadha. This
dynasty incorporated Avanti into the Magadha Empire.
The last dynasty of Magadha was the Nanda dynasty,
founded by Mahapadmananda, with Dhanananda as its
last ruler.

questions.explanation:
Varahamihira was a prominent astrologer and
astronomer of the Gupta period. He composed the
Panchasiddhantika, Brihad Jataka, Brihad Samhita, and

The karkhana system was quite developed

salaries, while those in the Gair-Ratibi received no fixed
salary. Firoz Shah Tughlaq provided substantial funds
to encourage production in these karkhanas.

Bengal, Bihar, Orissa, and the Banaras division of Uttar
Pradesh. Under this system, zamindars were recognized
as the owners of the land, and 10/11 of the total revenue
was assigned to the government.

Bengal made peace with Robert Clive
through the Treaty of Murshidabad

Clive's Jackal.

(E) The Battle of Buxar was fought between

(b) Only (A), (B) and (C)

questions.explanation:
After the Battle of Plassey, Mir Jafar's son
Miran assassinated Siraj-ud-Daula, the Nawab of
Bengal. Mir Jafar was known as "Colonel Clive's

Clive. J.Z. Hallwell, an eyewitness to the Black Hole
incident, gave the number of victims but did not name

the combined forces of Bengal, Awadh, and Delhi faced
Munro's British army. With the permission of Sultan
Shuja, the first British factory was established in
Hooghly, Bengal, in 1651.

struggle. In 1904, B.D. Savarkar founded the
organization Mitra Mela, which later transformed into
the Abhinav Bharat organization. Later, in 1900,
Savarkar moved to London.

questions.explanation:

in 1918. This flu spread throughout the country from
Indian soldiers stationed in the British Army in
Bombay. The Spanish Flu was a global pandemic in

This flu infected one-third of the world's population and
killed over 20 million people.

questions.questionText:
28. Consider the following statements about the
development of education in India in the 19th
century:

(A) The Charter Act of 1813 provided for an
annual expenditure of one lakh rupees for
education in India.

(B) Charles Wood's Dispatch on Education of
1854 declared that the objective of
educational policy was the teaching of
Eastern learning.

(C) The Hunter Education Commission was
formed in 1882-83 to examine the general
functioning of Indian universities.

(D) During the Oriental-Anglo Controversy,
the group of Orientalists was led by H.T.
Prinsep. He advocated for the progressive
use of Oriental literature.

Select the correct answer from the options
given below :
questions.explanation:
The Government of India Charter Act of
1813 first provided for an annual expenditure of 1 lakh
rupees on Indian education. The Wood Dispatch of
1854 further called for the spread of education in both
English and native languages. The Hunter Education
Commission, formed in 1882, focused on primary
education, not higher education. During the Anglo-
Oriental Education Controversy, H.T. Prinsep led the
group of Orientalists. He was in favor of promoting
Oriental literature.

against the taxes imposed by the British. According to
Abbe Vaire, in the 17th century, if anyone in the artisan
caste felt insulted, they would close their shops

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (Re-exam June 29.8.2024) S-I 504
questions.questionText:
30. In historiography, Ranke's approach to history
emphasizes the following :
questions.explanation:
Ranke's approach to history emphasizes the
sanctity of facts. Ranke had a profound influence on
Western historiography and is considered a symbol of
the quality of 19th-century German historical studies.
Ranke was adept at constructing narratives without
overstepping the boundaries of historical generality,
which is why he placed great emphasis on the sanctity
of facts.

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (Re-exam June 29.8.2024) S-I 504
questions.questionText:
31. Arrange the changing nature of archaeological
science/archaeological perspectives given below
in order from earliest to latest:

(A) New and process archaeology

(B) The generative model of evolution

(C) The diffusion perspective

(D) The indigenous archaeology of cultural

heritage

Select the correct answer from the options
given below :
questions.explanation:
Archaeology is the study of the ancient and
recent
human
past
through
material
remains.
Archaeology analyzes the material remains of the past
in search of a comprehensive understanding of human
culture. Archaeological perspectives can be organized
into new and process archaeology, the generative model
of evolution, and the indigenous archaeology of cultural
heritage

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (Re-exam June 29.8.2024) S-I 504
questions.questionText:
32. Which of the following Sufi saints translated
'Amrit Kund' under the name 'Bahrul Hayat'?
questions.explanation:
The Sufi saint Sheikh Muhammad Ghaus
translated the Amrit Kund into Persian in 1602, titled
Bahrul Hayat. It covers a wide range of topics,
including postures used for meditation. It is possibly the
first illustrated yoga textbook. The book depicts a yogi
performing 22 asanas

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (Re-exam June 29.8.2024) S-I 504
questions.questionText:
33. Where is the Tamil inscription, which records
the construction of a temple to Lord Shiva by a
merchant,
Samandaperumal
alias
Tavaschakravarthi, in 1281, located?
questions.explanation:
A Tamil inscription has been found in
Quanzhou, South China, which records the construction
of a temple to Lord Shiva by a merchant named
Samandaperumal alias Tavaschakravarti in 1281 AD. It
is noteworthy that Buddhism arrived in China from
India in ancient times. Even today, the number of
Buddhists in China is higher than in India.

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (Re-exam June 29.8.2024) S-I 504
questions.questionText:
34. In 1855-56, the ________ tribe of Bihar and
Bengal, armed with axes and bows and arrows,
temporarily overthrew British rule from their
region.
questions.explanation:
The Santhal tribal rebellion of 1855-56 was
the most powerful of the tribal uprisings. This rebellion
was mainly concentrated between Bhagalpur and
Rajmahal. The Santhal rebellion was led by two Santhal
brothers named Sidhu and Kanhu. The government
imposed martial law and crushed this rebellion, and
Sidhu and Kanhu were sentenced to death.

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (Re-exam June 29.8.2024) S-I 504
questions.questionText:
35. Identify the items exported from India to Rome
during the post-Mauryan period :

(A) Textiles
(B) Glass beads

(C) Ivory (gajdant)
(D) Olive oil

(E) Black pepper

Select the correct answer from the options
given below :
questions.explanation:
The most significant development in the
economic life of the post-Mauryan period was the
growing trade between India and Rome, as detailed in
Pliny's "Periplus of the Erythraean Sea," as well as in
excavations at Arikamedu, Uraiyur, and Pondicherry.
Among the items exported from India to Rome were
textiles, ivory, black pepper, etc., while India primarily
imported gold from Rome.

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (Re-exam June 29.8.2024) S-I 504
questions.questionText:
36. Who were the commanders of the army that
Alauddin Khilji sent to attack Warangal at the
end of 1302 or the beginning of the following
year, which was badly defeated?
questions.explanation:
At the end of 1302 or the beginning of the
following year, Alauddin Khilji sent a army under the
leadership of Fakhruddin Jauna and Chajju to attack
Warangal, which was badly defeated. Between 1309
and 1310, Malik Kafur attacked Warangal. Ultimately,
the ruler, Pratap Rudradeva, accepted Alauddin's
sovereignty on the terms of accepting his sovereignty
and paying regular tribute.

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (Re-exam June 29.8.2024) S-I 504
questions.questionText:
38. Traditionally, the number of Alvars and
Nayanars is :
questions.explanation:
Traditionally, the number of Alvars and
Nayanars was 12 and 63. In South India, during the 9th
and 10th centuries, Vaishnavite saints were called
Alvars, and Shaivite saints were called Nayanars.
Among the Alvar saints, Tirumangai, Periya, Andal,
and Namalvar were prominent, while among the
Nayanar saints, Appar, Tirugnana, Sambandar, and
Sundaramurthy were prominent. The collection of
verses by Nayanar saints is called Thirumudai.

questions.questionText:
42. Correct Matching Who propagated the concept
of "Total History"?
questions.explanation:
The concept of Total History was propagated
by Marc Block. Marc Block was primarily a French
historian and emphasized the need for a holistic
approach to historical study. Marc Block did not believe
in the factual study of history and believed that the
foundation of history lies in totality.

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (Re-exam June 29.8.2024) S-I 504
questions.questionText:
43. The author of the book "Nyaya Tatva," which
elaborates
on
the
philosophy
of
the
Vishishtadvaita school, is :
questions.explanation:
The author of the book "Nyaya Tatva," which
elaborates on the philosophy of the Vishishtadvaita
school, is Nathmuni. Nathmuni was a Vaishnava
theologian who compiled and compiled the Nalayira
Divya Prabandham. One of his works is Nathmuni
Yoga Rahasya. The Vishishtadvaita school was founded
by Ramanujacharya, who composed the Vedanta
Sangraha and a commentary on the Bhagavad Gita.

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (Re-exam June 29.8.2024) S-I 504
questions.questionText: 44. Mark the odd word from the following :
questions.explanation:
Arghatta, Vapi, and Nauriya are originally
related to water wheels or Persian wheels used for
irrigating land. It was usually driven by draft animals
such as oxen, buffaloes, or camels. It was used to draw
water from deep wells. Pulleys were primarily part of
architectural art.

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (Re-exam June 29.8.2024) S-I 504
questions.questionText:
45. The Jewish merchant Abraham ben Yizu
(1133-49) operated a bronze factory in which of
the following Indian cities?
questions.explanation:
The Jewish merchant Abraham ben Yizu
(1133-49 AD) operated a bronze factory in the Indian
city of Mangalore. Mangalore is an ancient and
medieval city located in Karnataka, whose excavations
have yielded numerous archaeological materials.

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (Re-exam June 29.8.2024) S-I 504
questions.questionText:
46. Traditionally, the five major Aryan tribes
included in the "Panchjana" are :
questions.explanation:
The Aryans were divided into several tribes.
The names of five tribes are often found: Puru, Yadu,
Turvas, Anu, and Duhyu. These are called the
Panchajanas. The ruler of a tribe was called a king. The
smallest unit of Aryan political organization was the
clan or family. In addition to the above five tribes,
mention is also found of five smaller tribes: Anil,
Paktha, Bhalanas, Shiva, and Vishanin.

questions.questionText:
49. Arrange the seaports mentioned in post-
Mauryan sources in the Indian subcontinent
from north to south :

(A) Barbaricum

(B) Barigaj (Bhrigukachchha)

(C) Muziris (Musiripatnam)

(D) Souppara (Sopara)

Select the correct answer from the options
given below :
questions.explanation:
The Greek text, Periplus of the Erythraean
Sea, describes India's trade activities and the ports on
India's eastern and western coasts. The seaports in
ancient India during the post-Mauryan period, in north
to
south
order,
are
Barbaricum,
Barigaj
(Bhrigukachchha), Sopara, and Muziris (Musiripatnam).
According to the Periplus, slave trade took place from
Bhrigukachchha, and Barbaricum was located at the
mouth of the Indus.

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (Re-exam June 29.8.2024) S-I 504
questions.questionText:
50. Which of the following texts contain the earliest
evidence of Radha as Krishna's devoted beloved?

(A) Ashtangahridayasangraha

(B) Geeta Govinda

(C) Harshacharita

(D) Brahmavaivarta Purana

Select the correct answer from the options
given below :
questions.explanation:
The texts containing the earliest evidence of
Radha as Krishna's beloved (priyatama) are the Geeta
Govinda and the Brahmavaivarta Purana. Geeta
Govinda is a book written by the 12th-century poet
Jayadeva, which describes the relationship between
Krishna, Radha, and the gopis of Vrindavan.
Brahmavaivarta Purana is the 10th Purana of the Vedic
tradition. It describes Radha's appearance after the
creation of the universe and Krishna's pastimes.

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (Re-exam June 29.8.2024) S-I 504
questions.questionText:
51. Which three of the following statements are
correct regarding famine?

(A) In
1880,
Lord
Lytton's
government
appointed the Strachey Commission

(B) Lord Curzon appointed a commission
headed by Sir Anthony Macdonell. It
submitted its report in 1901

(C) The famine of 1876–78 affected Madras,
Bombay, Uttar Pradesh, and Punjab

(D) The famine of 1866 affected Rajputana,
Punjab, Central Provinces, and Berar and
Marathwada

Select the correct answer from the options
given below :
questions.explanation:
In the context of famine, Lord Lytton formed
the Strachey Commission in 1880, which was the first
famine commission. In 1900, Lord Curzon formed a
Famine Commission under the chairmanship of
Anthony Macdonell, which submitted its report in 1901.
The famine of 1876-78 affected Madras, Bombay, Uttar
Pradesh, and Punjab. The famine of 1866 affected
Orissa, causing the death of 1 million people.

questions.questionText:
53. During the Mughal period, the ministry of
'Diwan-i-Buyutat' was concerned with which of
the following?
questions.explanation:
During the Mughal period, the ministry of
'Diwan-i-Buyutat' was concerned with Karkhanas
(State-governed factories). Its head was called Mir-i-
Sama. The Mir-i-Sama had independent charge of the
organization and management of the factories under the
empire. These factories often manufactured items
related to the emperor, which were mostly used in royal
households.

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (Re-exam June 29.8.2024) S-I 504
questions.questionText:
54. The meaning of the "Cleopatra's Nose"
principle in history is :
questions.explanation:
The meaning of the "Cleopatra's Nose"
principle in history is the relationship between cause
and effect. The Cleopatra's Nose principle in history
shows that insignificant factors can have profound
effects. This is an important idea for historians because
small differences in the context in which we form
causal inferences can have powerful effects.

questions.questionText:
59. According to the early Pali text Suttanipata,
cattle should be protected because they provide
us with :

(A) Food
(B) Strength
(C) Fertilizer

(D) Beauty
(E) Happiness

Select the correct answer from the options
given below :
questions.explanation:
According to the early Pali text Suttanipata,
cattle should be protected because they provide us with
food, strength, beauty, and happiness (annada, vanada,
sukhada). In fact, in the 6th century BCE, Animal
sacrifices began on a large scale in Vedic yagnas. On
the other hand, the need for animal protection was felt
during this period for advanced iron-based agriculture,
as expressed in the Buddhist text Suttanipata.

Bahmani kingdom take place?
questions.explanation:
The Battle of Kovilakonda between
Vijayanagara and the Bahmani kingdom took place
during the reign of Krishnadeva Raya, the ruler of
Vijayanagara. Krishnadeva Raya was one of the greatest
rulers of the Tuluva dynasty, during whose reign
Vijayanagara's glory reached its peak. His reign is
considered the classical era of Telugu literature. Eight
great Telugu scholars resided in his court. He composed
the Amuktamalyada, a Telugu epic poem.

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (Re-exam June 29.8.2024) S-I 504
questions.questionText:
62. In which month and year was the All India
States People's Conference founded?
questions.explanation:
The All India States People's Conference was
established in December 1927. It was also known as the
Praja Mandal. The main objective of the Praja Mandal
was to resolve the problems of various states by
building mutual consensus among them. Later,
Jawaharlal Nehru also chaired the Praja Mandal. The
first conference of the Praja Mandal was held in
Bombay in December 1927.

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (Re-exam June 29.8.2024) S-I 504
questions.questionText:
65. In the context of the Chola state, the distinction
between ceremonial sovereignty and actual
political control is indicative of the following :
questions.explanation:
The distinction between ceremonial
sovereignty and actual political control in the context of
the Chola state is indicative of the segmented state
model. Burton Stein was the first to propose the concept
of a segmented state in the context of South Indian
states. In the early medieval period, the most powerful
state in South India was that of the Cholas, who
promoted autonomy in local administration.

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (Re-exam June 29.8.2024) S-I 504
questions.questionText:
66. Which of the following statements are correct
regarding the status of women?

(A) Rashtrakuta king Amoghavarsha regularly
appointed courtesans as his envoys

(B) Princess Akkadevi of the Chalukya dynasty
assumed the governorship of the province

(C) Ibn Battuta observed thirteen (13) schools
for girls' education and twenty-three for
boys in Hanaur (South India)

(D) Varthema
(1505)
wrote
about
Vijayanagara that women went out with
their faces completely covered

Select the correct answer from the options
given below :
questions.explanation:
The status of women in early medieval South
India was better than that of women in North India. The
Rashtrakuta king Amoghavarsha regularly appointed
courtesans as his envoys. Akka Devi, a princess of the
Chalukya dynasty, ruled the Kishukadu province. She
was the sister of the Chalukya king Jayasimha II. Ibn
Battuta observed 13 schools for girls and 23 for boys in
Hanaur (South India). Purdah was prevalent among
women in Vijayanagara, but Varthema does not
mention it.

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (Re-exam June 29.8.2024) S-I 504
questions.questionText:
67. The Caesars and Pest History presents history
as follows:
questions.explanation:
The Caesars and Pest History presents history
as a mere compilation of historical facts. In this method,
facts are discovered through various means, hence it is
also called fact-finding. This method is mostly used in
schools, colleges, or historical research.

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (Re-exam June 29.8.2024) S-I 504
questions.questionText:
68. Against which of the following princely states
did the independent Republic of India launch
'Operation Polo'?
questions.explanation:
After independence, many princely states
merged with India, but states like Hyderabad favored
the status quo. The ruler of this state was Muslim, while
the majority of the population was Hindu. The Indian
government wanted the Nizam of Hyderabad to
voluntarily join the Indian Republic. However, when
negotiations failed, the Indian Army finally annexed
Hyderabad to India under Operation Polo on September
13, 1948.

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (Re-exam June 29.8.2024) S-I 504
questions.questionText:
69. Which of the following are associated with
types of marriage in ancient India?

(A) Ashvamedha
(B) Anuloma

(C) Vajpayee
(D) Pratiloma

Select the correct answer from the options
given below :
questions.explanation:
In ancient India, two types of marriages were
prevalent: Anuloma and Pratiloma. When a person of a
higher caste married a girl of a lower caste, it was called
Anuloma marriage, such as a Brahmin marrying a
Kshatriya girl. When a person of a lower caste married
a girl of a higher caste, it was called Pratiloma marriage,
such as a Shudra marrying a Brahmin girl.

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (Re-exam June 29.8.2024) S-I 504
questions.questionText:
70. Which of the following statements are correct
in the context of trade and commerce in the
medieval period?

(A) The Gujarat silk industry was completely
dependent on the import of raw silk from
China in the seventeenth century

(B) Bengal obtained opium from Bihar

(C) Gujarat obtained lac (lac) from Bengal for
the manufacture of lacquerware

(D) Bengal's manufacturers of conch shell
jewelry depended on the import of conch
shells from Tuticorin

Select the correct answer from the options
given below :
questions.explanation:
Trade and commerce in India was quite
developed during the medieval period, as detailed in the
writings of foreign travelers. During this period, Bengal
obtained opium from Bihar. Gujarat obtained lac (lac)
from Bengal for the manufacture of lacquerware.
Bengal manufacturers of conch shell jewelry relied on
the import of conch shells from Tuticorin. Silk
production in India was abundant in the 17th century,
and Gujarat was no longer dependent on China for silk.
During the period from 1680 to 1700, the Dutch East
India Company exported cotton textiles from Gujarat
and the Coromandel belt.

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (Re-exam June 29.8.2024) S-I 504
questions.questionText:
71. Which of the following statements are correct?

(A) Shaiva Siddhanta recognizes three eternal
principles—God (Shiva), the universe, and
the soul.

(B) The Agamas are considered authoritative
texts by followers of Shaiva Siddhanta,
Kashmiri Shaivism, and the Veerashaiva
tradition.

(C) The Kapalikas and Kalamukhis were the
two major Vaishnava sects.

(D) Vaishnava devotion became popular in
South India due to the ideas and activities
of the Nayanar saints.

Select the correct answer from the options
given below :
questions.explanation:
Kapalikas and Kalamukhas were the major
sects of Shaivism. The Nayanar saints popularized
Shaivism in South India. Shaiva Siddhanta recognizes
three eternal principles: God (Shiva), the universe, and
the soul. Furthermore, the Agamas composed by
followers of Shaiva Siddhanta, Kashmiri Shaivism, and
the Veerashaiva tradition are considered authoritative
texts.

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (Re-exam June 29.8.2024) S-I 504
questions.questionText:
72. The spirit of the Renaissance had a profound
impact on history writing. Which of the
following is not related to those influences?
questions.optionA: A return to a humanistic approach to history
questions.optionC:
The rise of a new school of humanistic
historians
questions.optionD:
The emergence of universal history and
chronology
questions.explanation:
The Renaissance began in Italy in the 16th
century and within a short period of time, it swept
across Europe. From a historical perspective, the
Renaissance highlighted the humanistic aspect of
history and established its importance, but it did not
contribute to the emergence of non-specialist historians.
It gave rise to a new school of humanistic historians and
brought about a change in people's historical
perspective.

questions.questionText:
74. Which of the following statements are correct
regarding Akbar's religious policy?

(A) He abolished the pilgrim tax

(B) He built the Ibadat Khana in Sikri in 1580

(C) He declared 'Mazhar' in 1579

(D) He started Din-i-Ilahi

Select the correct answer from the options
given below :
questions.explanation:
The fundamental objective of Mughal emperor
Akbar's religious policy was to establish universal
tolerance. He abolished the pilgrimage tax in 1563. He
built the Ibadat Khana in Fatehpur Sikri in 1575 and
proclaimed the Mazhar in 1579. In 1581-82, Akbar
introduced a new ideology called Din-i-Ilahi (Tauhid-i-
Ilahi), which some historians consider a new religion.

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (Re-exam June 29.8.2024) S-I 504
questions.questionText:
75. By 1800, the Maratha Empire had become a
confederation of five major chiefs. Who were
these five major chiefs?

(1) The Peshwa in Pune, the Gaekwad in
Baroda, the Scindias from Gwalior, the
Holkars in Indore, and the Bhonsles in
Nagpur.

(2) The Gaekwads in Pune, the Peshwa in
Baroda, the Holkars in Nagpur, the
Bhonsles in Indore, and the Scindias in
Gwalior.

(3) The Scindias in Gwalior, the Bhonsles in
Pune, the Gaekwads in Indore, the Holkars
in Baroda, and the Peshwas in Nagpur.

(4) The Scindias in Pune, the Peshwa in
Gwalior, the Holkars in Baroda, the
Gaekwads in Indore, and the Bhonsles in
Nagpur
questions.explanation:
The Maratha Empire was founded by
Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. Later, under the Peshwas,
the Maratha Empire became pan-Indian. By 1800, the
Maratha Empire had become a confederation of five
major chiefdoms: the Peshwas in Pune, the Gaekwads
in Baroda, the Scindias in Gwalior, the Holkars in
Indore, and the Bhonsles in Nagpur. The Maratha
Empire's history was marked by conflict with the
British.

questions.questionText:
77. Which of the following statements are correct
about the Great War of 1857?

(A) V.D. Savarkar called it a 'planned war of
national independence

(B) Savarkar tried to prove that the rebellions
of 1826-27, 1831-32, 1840, and 1854 were
precursors to the Great War of 1857

(C) T.R. Holmes propagated the view that the
1857 rebellion was a 'war of fanatic
religious fanatics against Christians

(D) James Outram and W. Taylor considered
this great war to be the result of a 'Hindu-
Muslim conspiracy

(E) L.E.R. Rees interpreted the Great War of
1857 as a 'struggle between civilization and
barbarism'

Select the correct answer from the options
given below :
questions.explanation:
The revolt of 1857 is called India's first war
of independence. V.D. Savarkar, in his 1909 book, *The
Indian War of Independence*, called it a national war of
independence. According to him, the revolts of 1826-
27, 1831-32, 1840, and 1854 were precursors to the
great war of 1857. Furthermore, L.E.R. Rees described
this revolt as a "war of fanatics against Christians," T.R.
Holmes called it a 'war between barbarism and
civilization' and James Outram and W. Taylor called it a
'Hindu-Muslim conspiracy'.

questions.questionText:
79. Consider the following statements about the
growth and development of painting in the 19th
and 20th centuries :

(A) The Calcutta School of Art was established

in 1854.

(B) Kalighat painting developed in the first

quarter of the 19th century.

(C) Abanindranath Tagore first painted Bharat

Mata in 1905.

(D) Ravi Varma's paintings were exhibited at

the Madras session of the Congress held in

1903, and around the same time, the

British awarded him the title of Vaisar-e-

Hind (1904).

Select the correct answer from the options
given below :
questions.explanation:
In the context of the growth and development
of painting in the 19th and 20th centuries, the Calcutta
School of Art was established in 1854. In 1905,
Abanindranath Tagore first painted the picture of Bharat
Mata. This painting depicts the Mother Goddess
providing education, food, and clothing. Ravi Varma's
paintings were exhibited at the Madras session of the
Congress held in 1903, and around the same time, the
British awarded him the title of Vaisar-e-Hind (1904).
Kalighat painting (Calcutta) was initiated by the Patua
community in the mid-19th century.

wrote three books on the science of music,
namely Sangeet Raga, Sangeet Mimansa, and
Surprabandha?
questions.explanation:
Rana Kumbha (Kumbhakarna) of Mewar
wrote three books on the science of music, namely
Sangeet Raga, Sangeet Mimansa, and Surprabandha. He

by Sarangdev. He commissioned the Kirti/Vijay Stambh
to be built in Chittor in 1448 AD. He also wrote a
commentary on Jayadeva's Gita Govinda, titled Rasik
Priya.

82. Who among the following captured the British
factory at Kasim Bazar during the Calcutta
Campaign and captured Fort William on June
20, 1756?
questions.explanation:
On June 4, 1756, Siraj-ud-Daulah attacked
and captured Kasimbazar, and then attacked Calcutta on
June 15. After a five-day siege in Calcutta, the Nawab
captured Fort William on June 20, 1756. Governor
Drake, Commander Minichin, and other British officers
were forced to flee and seek refuge on Fulta Island, and
most of the people were imprisoned in the fort. The
Black Hole incident is also related to this.

of his coronation?
questions.explanation:
On June 14, 1674, Shivaji had his coronation

Kashi, in Raigad. On this occasion, Shivaji assumed the
titles of Chhatrapati, Hindu Dharma Udvarak, Kshatriya
Kulavatash,

Singhasanadhishvara,
etc.
Shivaji did not assume the title of Vedmarga
Pratishthaapak. After his coronation, Shivaji's last
important campaign was the Karnataka campaign
(1677).

questions.questionText:
85. Who among the following said that history is
only science, nothing more and nothing less?
questions.explanation:
Views of various historians regarding the
philosophy of history: – J.B. Bury said, “History is only
science, nothing more and nothing less.” Seeley said,
“History is the politics of the past.” Spengler said,

Ali said, “A nation that ignores history has no future.”
Karl Marx said, “History repeats itself, first as tragedy,
then as farce.”

87. In ancient India, the word 'Takshan' signifies
which of the following?
questions.explanation:
In ancient India, the word takshana
(woodcutter) was used for a carpenter. Carpenters held
an important place in ancient economic life, as they
made all agricultural tools. Like other craftsmen in
ancient times, carpenters also had their own artisan
guild. They were sometimes required to perform forced
labor for the state.

questions.questionText:
88. Which of the following Sufi saints called
Hindus "Ahle Kitab" and the Vedas "God-
ordained (revealed) book"?
questions.explanation:
Sufi saint Mirza Mazhar Jan-e-Jana called
Hindus "Ahle Kitab" and the Vedas "God-ordained
(revealed) book." Mirza Mazhar Jan-i-Jana was a
renowned Naqshbandi Sufi saint. He founded the
Mazharia Shamsiya, a sub-sect of the Naqshbandi order.
Among his important disciples was the renowned
Hanafi scholar Qadi Thanaullah Panipati, who wrote a
commentary on the Quran, titled Tafsir-i Mazhari.

writings of Sukra, where he describes the king as both

92. In ancient texts, which of the following is
considered the "Talker of Kings"?
questions.explanation:
In ancient texts, Varuna is considered the
"Talker of Kings." Varuna was originally a Rigvedic
deity who is said to reside in a thousand pillars. Varuna
was also considered the controller of Rita. Varuna's
importance is extolled in the Rigveda, and he is
considered the supreme deity of the Rigvedic period,
second only to Indra. However, his importance later
diminished.

93. Which of the following books states that "the
king's status was similar to that of the soldiers;
both received separate remuneration and were
entitled to share the nation's wealth"?
questions.explanation:
The Arthashastra states that "the king's status
was similar to that of the soldiers; both received
separate remuneration and were entitled to share the
nation's wealth." The Arthashastra was written by
Kautilya, the Prime Minister of Emperor Chandragupta
Maurya. Kautilya considers the king to be the originator
of Dharma and says that the king should always be
available to his subjects.

94. The early Dharmasutras note that "the king is
essentially a servant, and the 16³ tax is his
remuneration." The Dharmasutras referred to
are :
questions.explanation:
The Baudhayana Dharmasutra notes that the
king is essentially a servant, and 16% taxes are his
remuneration. After the Gautama Dharmasutra, the
Baudhayana Dharmasutra is the oldest Dharmasutra.
The Dharmasutras primarily contain information on
social and religious rules. Baudhayana believed that the
king should receive a fixed tax in return for his service,
equal to 16% of the produce.

The Chapekar brothers were prominent

Hari Chapekar, Balkrishna Hari Chapekar, and Vasudev

B. Fragmentation

C. Continuity/Discontinuity

D. Intercontinuity

questions.optionA: Only A, B, C and D
questions.optionB: Only B, C, D and E

Postmodernism was a cultural movement in
the arts and philosophy that emerged in the second half
of the 20th century, challenging the prevailing

multidimensionality,

Praicois Lyotard is the founder of postmodernism.

2.
The main sources for the Arab invasion of
Sindh in the early eighth century are :
questions.explanation:
In 712 AD, the Arabs, led by Muhammad bin
Qasim, invaded Sindh. Information about this invasion
is found in the Chachnama, written in Arabic and
translated into Persian by Ali. At that time, Sindh was
ruled by Dahir, who was defeated by Muhammad bin
Qasim in the Battle of Rabar. The Arab conquest of
Sindh had a profound impact on India.

6.
By what name were self-cultivating farmers
known in Rajasthan?
questions.explanation:
In Rajasthan, self-cultivating farmers were
known as Gaveti. Self-cultivating farmers were those
who cultivated land in the village they lived in. They
had permanent and hereditary ownership of their land.
Self-cultivating farmers had the right to lease and sell
their land. They were also known as Malik-e-Zamin.

questions.questionText:
7.
Which of the following trade items was not
imported into India from the Western world?
questions.explanation:
The most prominent feature of the post-
Mauryan period in ancient India was the growth of trade
with the West. India's trade relations with Rome, the
Western world, were quite strong during this period.
India exported luxury goods to Rome, while Rome
imported wine, glassware, pearls, gold, and other items
from India. India did not import wood from the Western
world.
[Exam Date: 29.08.2024, Shift-II]

The Pax Britannica policy adopted by the
British during the first half of the 19th century
did not result in which of the following
phenomena?
questions.optionD: Restriction on moneylenders in rural areas
questions.explanation:
The Pax Britannica policy adopted by the
British during the first half of the 19th century appears
to have resulted in the suppression of the Pindaris, the
Thuggees, and the disbandment of irregular troops. The
ban on moneylenders in rural areas was not a
consequence of this policy. Moneylenders in rural areas
primarily earned interest by lending money to local
people.

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (Re-exam June 29.8.2024) S-II 523
questions.questionText:
9.
Which of the following is identified with the
Nasatyas of the Rigveda?
questions.explanation:
The Boghazkoi inscription, dated to 1400
BCE, recovered from Turkey in Asia Minor, mentions
four Rigvedic deities, including Indra, Mitra, Varuna,
and Nasatya. Nasatya here refers to the Ashvin deity.
This inscription describes a treaty between two
kingdoms, with the four gods presented as witnesses.
The Boghazkoi inscription was discovered by Wikler.

14. Which of the following statements are true
about the patriarchal-bureaucratic empire
model?

A. Stephen P. Blake used it to study the
nature of the Delhi Sultanate and the
Mughal Empire

B. Its political framework is based on Max
Weber's work on patriarchal state relations

C. Patriarchal dominance does not derive
from
the
patriarch's
authority
over
domestic affairs

D. It demands obedience to the office/position,
not to the individual

E. To rule successfully, a patriarchal ruler
must have loyal, disciplined soldiers

Select the correct answer from the options
below :
questions.explanation:
A patriarchal-bureaucratic empire is a system
in which bureaucrats of power are hereditarily selected.
This trend has been visible in India since the Gupta
period. Its political framework is based on Max Bever's
work on the patriarchal state. Its theory is that to rule
successfully, a patriarchal ruler must have loyal,
disciplined soldiers.

names?
questions.explanation:

Delhi Sultanate and was associated with the court of
Alauddin. He wrote in many poetic forms including
Ghazal, Masnavi, Qata, Rubai and he has made an
important contribution in the development of Ghazal.

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (Re-exam June 29.8.2024) S-II 523
questions.questionText:
24. Which of the following statements is true?

A. An
attractive
feature
of
Tughlaq
architecture is the sloping walls called
"batter"

B. This was used in all the buildings of the
Tughlaq dynasty

C. The Tughlaqs used only brown stone in
their buildings

D. In the buildings of Firoz Shah Tughlaq, a
thick layer of lime plaster was applied over
the rubble, which was later washed with
paint

E. A bell and chain are a striking example of
decoration found in all the buildings of
Firoz Shah Tughlaq

Select the correct answer from the options
given below :
questions.explanation:
A striking feature of Tughlaq architecture is
the "sloping walls," also known as "nipravan" or
"batter." The walls and turrets are similar to the
Egyptian pyramids, sloping inward. In Firoz Tughlaq's
buildings, a thick layer of lime plaster was applied over
the stones, which was later washed off with paint.

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (Re-exam June 29.8.2024) S-II 523
questions.questionText:
25. Sher Shah was given the responsibility of
governing which of the following parganas
during the lifetime of his father Hasan Khan?

A. Chandoi
B. Khawaspur C. Passi

D. Sasaram
E. Satyari

Select the correct answer from the options
given below :
questions.explanation:
Sher Shah was born in 1472 AD. His
childhood name was Farid. Sher Shah was given the
responsibility of governing the Khawaspur and Sasaram
parganas during the lifetime of his father Hasan Khan.
Later, he defeated Humayun at Chausa and Kannauj and
became the emperor of India. Sher Shah's main
achievements were in the administrative and revenue
fields.

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (Re-exam June 29.8.2024) S-II 523
questions.questionText:
26. Which of the following Ajanta caves depicts
Indra and his entourage flying while greeting
Lord Buddha in the Tushita heaven?
questions.explanation:
Cave 17 at Ajanta depicts Indra and his
entourage flying while greeting Lord Buddha in the
Tushita heaven. Ajanta has a total of 29 caves, most of
which are related to Buddhism. Cave 17 is believed to
have been built during the Gupta-Vakataka period. Cave
1 at Ajanta is considered the latest, dating back to the
7th century AD.

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (Re-exam June 29.8.2024) S-II 523
questions.questionText:
27. Which of the following were military outposts
under the Delhi Sultanate to protect the
northwestern border during the Mongol
invasion?

A. Dipalpur
B. Debal
C. Lahore

D. Kasur
E. Multan

Select the correct answer from the options
given below :
questions.explanation:
Military outposts were established in
Dipalpur,
Lahore,
and
Multan
to
protect
the
northwestern border during the Mongol invasion under
the Delhi Sultanate. The Mongols invaded several times
during the Delhi Sultanate, with the most frequent
attacks occurring during the reign of Alauddin Khilji.
Balban was the first to establish several important
outposts in the northwestern region.

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (Re-exam June 29.8.2024) S-II 523
questions.questionText:
28. Which of the following items was not
commonly
found
in
copper
hoards/
assemblages?
questions.explanation:
Primitive axes, Fish-shaped swords, Horn-
shaped swords, etc. are commonly found in copper
hoards. Hand-axes are not commonly found in copper
hoards. Hand-made polished axes are found primarily in
Neolithic sites. Copper hoards primarily indicate the
Chalcolithic period, in which copper-made tools
predominated.

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (Re-exam June 29.8.2024) S-II 523
questions.questionText:
29. Which of the following statements are true
about the Justice Party?

A. The Justice Party was formed in 1916 with
a non-Brahmin manifesto

B. The party opposed the Congress party,
calling it a Brahmin-dominated organization

C. The Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms of 1919
allocated 50 reserved seats
to non-
Brahmins
in
the
Madras
Legislative
Council

D. The formation of the Ministry in 1920 was
the culmination of the Justice Party's
rebellion

E. After the 1926 electoral defeat at the hands
of the Swarajists, non-Brahmins left the
party and joined the Congress

Select the correct answer from the options
below :
questions.optionC: Only A, B, C and D
questions.optionD: Only A, B, D and E
questions.explanation:
In 1916-17, Mr. P. Tyagaraja and Naicker
formed the first non-Brahmin organization, the South
Indian Liberal Association, which later came to be
known as the Justice Party. This party opposed the
Congress, calling it a Brahmin-dominated organization.
The formation of the Ministry in 1920 was the
culmination of the Justice Party's rebellion. After losing
to the Swarajists in 1926, the non-Brahmins left the
party and joined the Congress.

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (Re-exam June 29.8.2024) S-II 523
questions.questionText:
30. Who among the following painted a watercolor
Sarang for Lady Impey?
questions.explanation:
Sheikh Zain al-Din painted a watercolor
Sarang for Lady Impey. In the latter half of the 18th
century, Sheikh worked under Mary Impey, wife of
Elijah Impey, Chief Justice of the Calcutta Supreme
Court. From 1777 to 1782, Sheikh used Hightman art
paper manufactured in England for his transparent
watercolor paintings.

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (Re-exam June 29.8.2024) S-II 523
questions.questionText:
31. Which of the following are true about the
Provisional Azad Hind Government?

A. The Provisional Azad Hind Government
was
declared
with
headquarters
in
Singapore

B. Subhas Chandra Bose became the Prime
Minister of this government

C. S.A. Iyer was a minister in this government

D. A.C. Chatterjee was a minister in this
government

E. Lakshmi Swaminathan was a minister in
this government

Select the correct answer from the options
given below :
questions.optionC: Only A, B, C and D
questions.explanation:
On October 21, 1943, Subhash Chandra Bose
formed the Provisional Government of Free India in
Singapore. In this Provisional Government, Subhash
Chandra Bose was the Prime Minister, while S.C.
Chatterjee was the Finance Minister, M.A. Iyer was the
Propaganda Minister, and Lakshmi Swaminathan was
the Minister of Women's Affairs. Subhash Chandra
Bose established the headquarters of the Provisional
Government in Rangoon, and it was supported by the
governments of Germany and Japan.

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (Re-exam June 29.8.2024) S-II 523
questions.questionText:
32. What is a megalithic trench tomb with a single
large vertical stone slab called?
questions.explanation:
Megalithic pit tombs with a single large
vertical stone slab are called menhirs. Menhirs are
granite stones, carved from a single stone. They can
reach up to
1
12 –
1
2 2 meter in length and are buried
vertically in a north-south direction near the tombs.
Menhirs are found in Europe, Africa, and Asia, and
after the Neolithic period, they are found in various
places in South India.

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (Re-exam June 29.8.2024) S-II 523
questions.questionText:
33. When the laying of railway lines in India was
beginning in 1853, who among the following
remarked, "This is the true forerunner of
modern industry"?
questions.explanation:
When the laying of railway lines in India was
beginning in 1853, Karl Marx remarked, "This is the
true forerunner of modern industry." Railways in India
developed during the reign of Governor General Lord
Dalhousie. The development of railways had both
positive and negative impacts on the Indian economy.

questions.questionText:
35. Due to the military reorganization, how much
increase was recorded in defense expenditure
as a share of total central and provincial
government revenue in India?
questions.explanation:
Military discontent was considered the
primary cause of the 1857 rebellion. Therefore, when
the army was reorganized after the suppression of the
1857 rebellion, defense expenditures in India increased
by 25% to 30% of total central and provincial
government revenues. This military reorganization
reduced the number of Indian troops and increased the
number of British troops.

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (Re-exam June 29.8.2024) S-II 523
questions.questionText:
36. Who among the following remarked in the
early nineteenth century, “A Hindu woman can
go anywhere alone, even into the most crowded
places, and need not fear the evil glances and
taunts of idlers… A house inhabited only by
women is a sanctuary which even the most
shameless person would not think of violating.”
questions.explanation:
In the early 19th century, Abbe J.A. Dubois
remarked, "A Hindu woman can go anywhere alone,
even in the most crowded places, and need not fear the
evil glances and lewd remarks of idlers. A house
inhabited only by women is a sanctuary which even the
most shameless person would not think of violating."

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (Re-exam June 29.8.2024) S-II 523
questions.questionText:

wrote
“Chaitanyacharitramita,”
a
biography
of
the
Vaishnava
saint
Chaitanyadeva?
questions.explanation:
"Chaitanya Charitamrita," the biography of
the Vaishnav saint Chaitanyadev, was written by
Krishnadas Kaviraj. Chaitanya Charitamrita literally
means "The Character of the Living Power in
Immortality." It is a remarkable transcendental work of
literature, containing over 11,000 verses and divided
into parts. Its influence is most visible in Bengal,
Orissa, and Manipur.

questions.questionText:
41. Who among the following was the Acharya of
the Ajivika sect?

A. Puran Kashyap

B. Mallinath

C. Pakudha Katyayana

D. Neminath

E. Ghosala Maskariputra

Select the correct answer from the options
given below :
questions.optionC: Only A, C, D and E
questions.explanation:
The Ajivika sect was founded by Makkhali
Putta Gosala. Gosala's philosophy is considered
fatalistic. Puran Kashyap and Pugudha Katyayana were
initially associated with the Ajivika sect. Later, Puran
Kashyap became a staunch inactionist, while Pugudha
Katyayana's philosophy is considered a nithyavadi one.

questions.testName: NTA UGC NET/JRF History Paper II (Re-exam June 29.8.2024) S-II 523
questions.questionText: 42. Which region was the Kubrawiyya Silsila active?
questions.explanation:
The Kubrawiyya Silsila was most active in
Kashmir. It was also active in eastern India. Mir Syed
Ali Hamdani is a prominent poet of this Silsila. The
main teachings of the Kubrawiyya sect were repentance,
renunciation, faith, solitude, and focusing on Allah.
They believed that remembering Allah is a way to
understand spiritual philosophy.
